children.translated_text: In the twenty-ninth [chapter], for the purpose of the <s>rāsa</s> [dance], the exchanges of words between <s>Hari</s>
and the <s>gopīs</s>, the commencement of the <s>rāsa</s> [dance], and the wonder of His disappearance. // 1 //
He who destroys the pride of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), whose own pride swells from conquering <s>Brahmā</s> and all others —
victorious is <s>Śrīpati</s> (the Lord of <s>Śrī</s>), the ornament of the circle of the <s>gopīs'</s> <s>rāsa</s> dance. // 2 //

body.text:
BhP_10,29.01
śrīśuka uvāca
bhagavān api tā rātṛīḥ śāradotphullamallikāḥ[*1] / vīkṣya rantuṃ manaś cakre yogamāyām upāśritaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.1. <s>Śrī Śuka</s> said: The <s>Bhagavān</s> (Blessed Lord) too, beholding those autumn nights with <s>mallikā</s> (jasmine) flowers in full bloom, made his mind [inclined] to enjoy, having resorted to <s>Yogamāyā</s> (his divine power of illusion). //

body.text: [*1] śarado mallikāvikasahetutvābhāve 'pi hetutvoktyā 'bhinavatvaṃ tena ca sarvapuṣpavikāso vyajyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Although autumn is not the natural cause for jasmine blossoming, by stating it as the cause, the unprecedented nature [of the event] is expressed, and thereby the blossoming of all flowers is implied.

body.text: nanu viparītam idam, paradāravinodena kandarpavijetṛtvapratīteḥ | maivam, "yogamāyām upāśritaḥ," "ātmārāmo 'py arīramat," "sākṣān manmathamanmathaḥ," "ātmany avaruddha-saurataḥ," ity ādiṣu svātantryābhidhānāt | tasmād rāsakrīḍāviḍambanaṃ kāmavijayakhyāpanāyety eva tattvam | kiṃ ca śṛṅgārakathāpadeśena viśeṣato nivṛttipareyaṃ pañcādhyāyīti vyaktīkariṣyāmaḥ | tā rātrīḥ "yātābalā vrajaṃ siddhā mayemā raṃsyatha kṣapāḥ" iti pratiśrutā ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.1||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Now, is this not contradictory — since dalliance with others' wives would suggest subjection to Cupid rather than victory over him? Not so, because in passages such as 'having resorted to <s>Yogamāyā</s>,' 'though self-delighting, he sported,' 'the <s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid) of <s>Manmatha</s> himself,' and 'one whose amorous pleasure is contained within himself' — his sovereignty is declared. Therefore, the truth is that the theatrical display of the <s>rāsa</s> dance is precisely for the proclamation of the conquest of desire. Moreover, we shall make clear that this group of five chapters (<s>pañcādhyāyī</s>), under the guise of an erotic narrative, is especially oriented toward renunciation. 'Those nights' — the meaning is: [those nights] that had been promised [to the <s>gopīs</s>] by the words 'Go back to <s>Vraja</s>, O accomplished women; you shall sport with me on these nights.' //

children.text: tadoḍurājaḥ kakubhaḥ karair mukhaṃ prācyā vilimpann aruṇena śantamaiḥ /
children.translated_text: Then the king of stars (the moon), soothing with his most gentle rays, rose in the east, anointing the face of the eastern quarter with his reddish [glow],

children.text: sa carṣaṇīnām udagāc chuco mṛjan priyaḥ priyāyā iva dīrghadarśanaḥ //
children.translated_text: like a long-absent beloved [anointing] the face of his darling — dispelling the sorrows of all people. //

body.text: tadā tasminn eva kṣaṇe tatpratītaye uḍurājaś candra udagād uditaḥ | kiṃ kurvan | dīrghakālena darśanaṃ yasya sa priyaḥ svapriyāyā mukham aruṇena kuṅkumena yathā vilimpati tathā prācyāḥ kakubho diśo mukhaṃ śantamaiḥ sukhatamaiḥ karai raśmibhir aruṇenodayarāgeṇa vilimpann aruṇīkurvann ity arthaḥ | sa prasiddha uḍurājaḥ | tathā carṣaṇināṃ janānāṃ śucas tāpaglānīr mṛjann apanayan ||BhPC_10,29.2||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] At that very moment, to make [the scene] palpable, the king of stars — the moon — rose. In what manner? Like a beloved who has not been seen for a long time, anointing the face of his beloved with reddish <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) — so [the moon] anointed the face of the eastern quarter with its most gentle, most pleasing rays, reddish with the glow of rising. That renowned king of stars, dispelling — removing — the sorrows, the heat-born weariness, of all people. //

children.translated_text: Seeing the moon — causing the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus) to bloom, with an unbroken disc, shining like the face of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), reddish as fresh <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron),

children.text: vanaṃ ca tatkomalagobhī rañjitaṃ jagau kalaṃ vāmadṛśāṃ manoharam //
children.translated_text: and seeing the forest colored by its gentle rays, He sang melodiously, captivating the minds of the doe-eyed women. //

body.text: kumut kumudaṃ vikasanīyaṃ vidyate yasya taṃ kumudvantam | na khaṇḍaṃ maṇḍalaṃ yasya tam | ramāyā ānanasyābheva ābhā yasya tam | navakuṅkumam ivāruṇam evaṃvidhaṃ candraṃ dṛṣṭvā | tathā vanaṃ ca tasya komalair gobhī raśmibhī rañjitaṃ dṛṣṭvā kalaṃ madhuraṃ jagau agāyata | katham | vāmadṛśāṃ vāmā manoharā dṛśo yāsāṃ tāsāṃ manoharaṃ yathā ||BhPC_10,29.3||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] '<s>Kumudvat</s>' — that which causes the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotus) to bloom. 'Of unbroken disc.' 'Whose radiance is like the face of <s>Ramā</s>.' 'Reddish as fresh <s>kuṅkuma</s>' — seeing such a moon, and seeing the forest colored by its gentle rays, He sang melodiously. In what manner? In a way that captivated the minds of the doe-eyed women. //

children.text: niśamya gītāṃ tad anaṅgavardhanaṃ vrajastriyaḥ kṛṣṇagṛhītamānasāḥ /
children.translated_text: Hearing that song, which increased [the fever of] love (<s>anaṅga</s>), the women of <s>Vraja</s>, whose minds were seized by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: ājagmur anyonyam alakṣitodyamāḥ sa yatra kānto javalolakuṇḍalāḥ //
children.translated_text: came [running], their efforts unnoticed by one another, their earrings swinging with their haste, to where their beloved was. //

body.text: asāpatnyāyānyonyam alakṣito na jñāpita udyamo yābhis tāḥ | sa kānto yatra tatra gītadhvani-mārgeṇa ājagmuḥ[*2] | javena vegena lolāni cañcalāni kuṇḍalāni yāsāṃ tāḥ ||BhPC_10,29.4||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Their efforts unnoticed by one another' — those whose haste was not made known to each other, [for they came] independently. They came to where the beloved was, following the trail of the song's sound. 'Their earrings swinging with their haste' — those whose earrings were restless due to the speed [of their running]. //

body.text: [*2] jagmur iti vaktavye ājagmur ity uktiḥ śukasya kṛṣṇāntike svāvasthānasphūrteḥ ||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] The use of '<s>ājagmuḥ</s>' (they came toward) instead of '<s>jagmuḥ</s>' (they went) reflects <s>Śuka's</s> spontaneous awareness of his own presence near <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. //

children.translated_text: Some came while milking, leaving the milking unfinished, eager [to go];
others left after placing milk on the fire for <s>saṃyāva</s> (wheat-cake), without removing it. //

body.text: [*3] aparā iti pūrveṇa pareṇāpy anveti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Others' — this word applies both to what precedes and what follows.

body.text: śrīkṛṣṇasūcakaśabdaśarvaṇena tatpravaṇacittānāṃ tatkṣaṇam eva traivargikakarmanivṛttiṃ dyotayantya ivārdhāvasitaṃ karma vihāya yayuḥ | tad āha-duhantya iti | payaḥ sthālīsthaṃ cullyām adhiśrityaitat kvāthamapratīkṣamānāḥ kāścid yayuḥ | saṃyāvaṃ godhūmakaṇānnaṃ pakvam anudvāsyānuttārya ||BhPC_10,29.5|| ||BhPC_10,29.6||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Upon hearing the sound indicative of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, those whose minds were inclined toward Him, as if to demonstrate the immediate cessation of all worldly activities at that very moment, abandoned their tasks half-done and went. This is stated: 'while milking' and so on. Some left after placing milk in a pot on the stove, without waiting for it to boil. '<s>Saṃyāva</s>' — a food made from wheat-grain, cooked but not removed [from the fire]. //

children.translated_text: Some who were applying cosmetics, some who were cleansing [their bodies], some who were applying collyrium to their eyes —
some went to <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> vicinity with their garments and ornaments in disarray. //

body.text: [*4] limpantyaḥ aṅgarāgaṃ kurvatyaḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Applying cosmetics' — applying body-ointment.

body.text: anyāḥ pramṛjantyaḥ aṅgodvartanādi kurvantyaḥ | kāśca kāścit kṛṣṇatuṣṭyarthaṃ karma tadāsaktam anasāmanyathā kṛtam api phalaty eveti dyotayann āha-vyatyasteti | sthānataḥ svarūpataś cordhvādhodhāraṇena viparyayaṃ prāptāni vastrābharaṇāni yāsāṃ tāḥ ||BhPC_10,29.7||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Others cleansing' — doing body-scrubbing and so forth. 'Some' — certain ones. Indicating that actions performed for <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> pleasure bear fruit even if done improperly due to [their] attachment to Him, he says: 'with [garments and ornaments] in disarray' — those whose garments and ornaments were transposed from their proper place and form, worn upside-down or reversed. //

body.text:
BhP_10,29.08
tā vāryamāṇāḥ patibhiḥ pitṛbhir bhrātṛbandhubhiḥ / govindāpahṛtātmāno na nyavartanta mohitāḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.8. They, being restrained by husbands, fathers, brothers, and kinsmen, yet their souls stolen by <s>Govinda</s>, did not turn back, being enchanted. //

body.text: na ca kṛṣṇākṛṣṭamanasāṃ vighnāḥ prabhavantīty āha-tā vāryamāṇā iti ||BhPC_10,29.8||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Obstacles have no power over those whose minds are drawn by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — this is stated: 'they, being restrained...' //

children.translated_text: Some <s>gopīs</s>, confined within their homes, unable to find a way out,
meditated upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, absorbed in contemplation of Him, with closed eyes. //

body.text: [*5] mudritanetrāḥ, yadvā mīlitaṃ locanam anyāśeṣajñānaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'With closed eyes' — with shut eyes; or, those for whom all other knowledge was dissolved.

body.text: na labdho nirgamo yābhis tāḥ | prāg api tadbhāvanāyuktās tadā nitarāṃ dadhyur ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.9||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Those who could not find a way out. Even before, they were absorbed in contemplation of Him; now, all the more so they meditated — this is the meaning. //

children.translated_text: Through the intense burning of the unbearable separation from their most beloved, their sins were destroyed;
through the bliss of the embrace of <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) attained in meditation, their [stock of] merit was exhausted. //
United with that very Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>), even though with the understanding of a paramour,
they immediately abandoned their material bodies made of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature), their bonds being completely dissolved. //

body.text: kiṃ ca tadānīm evaṃ taṃ paramātmānaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dhyānataḥ prāptāḥ satyo guṇamayaṃ dehaṃ jahur ity āha ślokadvayena-duḥsaheti | nanu kathaṃ jahuḥ paramātmeti jñānābhāvād ity āśaṅkyāha-jārabuddhyāpīti | na hi vastuśaktir buddhim apekṣate | anyathā matvāpi pītāmṛtavad iti bhāvaḥ | nanu tad api prārabdhakarmabandhane sati kathaṃ jahus tatrāha-sadyaḥ prakṣīṇa-bandhanā iti | nanu kathaṃ bhogam antareṇa prārabdhaṃ karma kṣīṇaṃ bhogenaiva sadyaḥ kṣīṇam ity āha-duḥsaheti | duḥsaho yaḥ preṣṭhavirahas tena tīvras tāpas tena dhutāni gatāny aśubhāni yāsām | tadaprāptiparamaduḥkhabhogena pāpaṃ kṣīṇam ity arthaḥ | tathā dhyānena prāptā acyutasya āśleṣeṇa yā nirvṛtiḥ paramasukhabhogas tayā kṣīṇaṃ maṅgalaṃ puṇyabandhanaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ | ato dhyānena paramātmaprāptes tatkālasukhaduḥkhābhyāṃ niḥśeṣakarmakṣayād guṇamayaṃ dehaṃ jahur iti ||BhPC_10,29.10|| ||BhPC_10,29.11||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Moreover, at that very time, having attained <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self, through meditation, they abandoned their material bodies — this is stated in the two verses beginning with 'unbearable.' Now, how did they abandon [their bodies] without the knowledge 'He is the Supreme Self'? Anticipating this, he says: 'even with the understanding of a paramour' — for the potency of the reality does not depend on [correct] understanding; just as one who drinks nectar thinking it to be something else [still benefits]. Now, how did they abandon [their bodies] when the bond of <s>prārabdha karma</s> (karma already in effect) remained? To this he says: 'their bonds being completely dissolved at once.' But how was <s>prārabdha karma</s> exhausted without [its natural] fruition? It was exhausted immediately through experience — this he states: 'unbearable' — the intense burning of the unbearable separation from their most beloved destroyed their sins. By the supreme suffering of not attaining Him, sin was exhausted — this is the meaning. And through the bliss — the supreme joy — of the embrace of <s>Acyuta</s> attained through meditation, the merit — the bond of good deeds — of those [<s>gopīs</s>] was exhausted. Thus, through the attainment of the Supreme Self via meditation, through the complete exhaustion of all <s>karma</s> by the pleasures and pains of that time, they abandoned their bodies made of the <s>guṇas</s>. //

body.text:
[*6] atra "jighāṃsayāpi haraye" ity atreva jārabuddhyāpīty apinā tādṛśabuddher nindyatvaṃ vyajya vastumahimnātiprāśastyaṃ vyañjitam |
[*7] guṇamayaṃ dehaṃ jahur ity uktyā cinmayadehena golokādau tatprāptir dhvanyate |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Here, by 'even with the understanding of a paramour' — by the word 'even,' such understanding is indicated as blameworthy, while the surpassing praiseworthiness [of the result] due to the greatness of the reality is implied. By the statement 'they abandoned the body made of <s>guṇas</s>,' their attainment [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] in <s>Goloka</s> and elsewhere with a spiritual body (<s>cinmayadehena</s>) is suggested.

children.translated_text: The king said:

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ viduḥ paraṃ kāntaṃ na tu brahmatayā mune /
children.translated_text: 'They knew <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as merely their beloved, not as <s>Brahman</s>, O sage;
how then could the cessation of the flow of <s>guṇas</s> (material qualities) occur for them, who were of material understanding?' //

body.text: [*8] ato guṇadhiyāṃ śrīkṛṣṇaguṇaikānubaddhapremamayīnāṃ tāsāṃ guṇapravāhoparamaḥ cinmayaguṇaparam-parāśrayasya cidvigrahasyoparamaḥ sāyujyamuktiḥ brahmopāsakānām iva katham iti |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Therefore, for those of material understanding — those whose love was exclusively attached to the qualities of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — how could the cessation of the flow of qualities, meaning the cessation attained through the spiritual form whose nature is a succession of spiritual qualities, that is, the <s>sāyujya</s> (identity) liberation like that of worshippers of <s>Brahman</s>, [be possible]?

body.text: nanu yathā patiputrādīnāṃ vastuto brahmatve' pi na tadbhajanān mokṣas tathā buddhyabhāvād evaṃ kṛṣṇe 'pi brahmabuddhyabhāvena tatsaṅgatiḥ kathaṃ mokṣahetur iti śaṅkate-kṛṣṇaṃ vidur iti | paraṃ kevalaṃ kāntaṃ kamanīyam ||BhPC_10,29.12||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] Just as worship of husband, son, and the like does not lead to liberation even though they are in reality <s>Brahman</s>, due to the absence of such understanding — so too, in the case of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, how can association with Him be the cause of liberation without the understanding of [His] <s>Brahman</s>-nature? — [the king] raises this doubt: 'They knew <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>...' 'Merely' (<s>param</s>) means 'only'; 'beloved' (<s>kānta</s>) means desirable. //

children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: uktaṃ purastād etat te caidyaḥ siddhiṃ yathā gataḥ /
children.translated_text: 'This has been explained to you before — how <s>Caidya</s> (<s>Śiśupāla</s>) attained perfection,
even though he hated <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, lord of the senses); how much more so then those dear to <s>Adhokṣaja</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is beyond the senses)?' //

body.text: pariharati-uktam iti | ayaṃ bhāvaḥ-jīveṣv āvṛtaṃ brahmatvaṃ kṛṣṇasya tu hṛṣīkeśatvād anāvṛtam ato na tatra buddhyapekṣeti ||BhPC_10,29.13||
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] He resolves [the doubt]: 'This has been explained.' The purport is: the <s>Brahman</s>-nature of individual souls (<s>jīvas</s>) is concealed, but that of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, due to His being <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (the lord of the senses), is not concealed; therefore, understanding is not required in His case. //

children.text: nṛṇāṃ niḥśreyasārthāya vyaktir bhagavato nṛpa / avyayasyāprameyasya[*9] nirguṇasya guṇātmanaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'The manifestation of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, O king, for the supreme good of human beings —

body.text: [*9] aprameyasyāparicchinnasya |
body.translated_text: [Commentary:] 'Of the immeasurable' — of the unlimited.

body.text: nanu dehī katham anāvṛtaḥ syād ata āha-nṛṇām iti | guṇātmano guṇaniyantuḥ | bhagavata evaṃrūpā abhivyaktir ato na dehasādṛśyam atra vaktuṃ yujyata iti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.14||
body.translated_text: Now, how can an embodied being be uncovered? To this he says — '<s>nṛṇām</s>' etc. | '<s>guṇātmanaḥ</s>' means the controller of the <s>guṇas</s>. | Of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, such a manifestation [occurs], therefore it is not appropriate here to speak of similarity with [an ordinary] body — this is the meaning.

children.text: kāmaṃ krodhaṃ bhayaṃ sneham aikyaṃ sauhṛdam eva ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (desire), <s>krodha</s> (anger), <s>bhaya</s> (fear), <s>sneha</s> (affection), <s>aikya</s> (unity), and <s>sauhṛda</s> (friendship) —

children.text: nityaṃ harau vidadhato[*10] yānti tanmayatāṃ[*11] hi te //
children.translated_text: those who constantly direct these toward <s>Hari</s> indeed attain oneness with him. //

body.text:
[*10] "vidadhate" iti pāṭhaḥ |
[*11] tanmayatāṃ tatsāyujyasārūpyādimuktiṃ tadekasphūrtiṃ ca |
body.translated_text: [*10] The reading '<s>vidadhate</s>' [is also found]. | [*11] '<s>tanmayatāṃ</s>' means liberation in the form of <s>sāyujya</s> (absorption), <s>sārūpya</s> (having the same form), etc., and also the manifestation of exclusive awareness of Him.

body.text: ato yathā kathañcit tadāsaktir muktikāraṇam ity āha-kāmam iti | aikyaṃ saṃbandham | sauhṛdaṃ bhaktim ||BhPC_10,29.15||
body.translated_text: Therefore, attachment to Him in any manner whatsoever is the cause of liberation — this he states with '<s>kāmam</s>' etc. | '<s>Aikyam</s>' means relationship. | '<s>Sauhṛdam</s>' means devotion. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.15 ||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.16
na caivaṃ vismayaḥ kāryo bhavatā bhagavaty aje / yogeśvareśvare kṛṣṇe yata etad vimucyate //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.16 — Nor should there be such wonder on your part regarding the unborn <s>Bhagavān</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lord of the lords of <s>yoga</s>, from whom this [whole world] is liberated. //

body.text: na ca bhagavato 'yam atibhāra ity āha-na caivam iti | yataḥ śrīkṛṣṇād etat sthāvarādikam api vimucyate ||BhPC_10,29.16||
body.translated_text: Nor is this too great a burden for the <s>Bhagavān</s> — he says '<s>na caivam</s>' etc. | Because from <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, even immovable beings and others are liberated. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.16 ||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.17
tā dṛṣṭvāntikam āyātā bhagavān vrajayoṣitaḥ / avadad vadatāṃ śreṣṭho vācaḥpeśair vimohayan //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.17 — Having seen those women of <s>Vraja</s> who had come near, the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the best of speakers, spoke, bewildering them with eloquent words. //

body.text: prastutam[*12] āha-tā dṛṣṭveti | vācaḥpeśair vāgvilāsaiḥ ||BhPC_10,29.17||
body.translated_text: He states the main narrative — '<s>tā dṛṣṭvā</s>' etc. | '<s>Vācaḥpeśaiḥ</s>' means with charming speech. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.17 ||

body.text: [*12] rasamayarāsalīlāprasaṅge īdṛśas te praśnaḥ samādhānaprapañcaś ca rasavighātakatvād anucita iti vyañjayan svayam evotkaṇṭhayā prastauti ||
body.translated_text: [*12] In the context of the rasa-filled <s>Rāsa</s> dance, such a question and elaborate resolution would be inappropriate as it would disrupt the <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment) — suggesting this, he himself, with longing, introduces [the topic]. ||

children.translated_text: The Blessed Lord spoke:

children.text: svāgataṃ vo mahābhāgāḥ priyaṃ kiṃ karavāṇi vaḥ /
children.translated_text: Welcome to you, O greatly fortunate ones! What dear thing shall I do for you?
Is all well in <s>Vraja</s>? Tell me the reason for your coming. //

body.text: sarvāḥ sasaṃbhramam āgatā vilokya sabhayam ivāha-vrajasyeti ||BhPC_10,29.18||
body.translated_text: Seeing all of them arriving in agitation, he speaks as if with concern — '<s>vrajasya</s>' etc. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.18 ||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.19
rajany eṣā ghorarūpā[*13] ghorasattvaniṣevitā / pratiyāta vrajaṃ neha stheyaṃ strībhiḥ sumadhyamāḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.19 — This night is of terrible form, frequented by terrible creatures. Go back to <s>Vraja</s>! Women should not stay here, O slender-waisted ones! //

body.text: [*13] yadvā aghorarūpā candrodayena tamohānāt, ato jyotsnayā dinaprāyatvād aghoraiḥ sattvair bhṛṅgakokilādyair niṣevitā, athavā ghoraṃ duṣṭānāṃ bhayajanakaṃ sattvaṃ balaṃ yasya tena mayā niṣevitā | ataḥ sarvathā vrajaṃ na yāta | prārthanāyāṃ loṭ | ittham evāgre mā vicinvanti, mā yāta ity ādi yojyam |
body.translated_text: [*13] Alternatively, '<s>aghorarūpā</s>' — not of terrible form, because darkness is removed by the rising of the moon; therefore, because of the moonlight it is almost like day, frequented by non-terrible creatures such as bees, cuckoos, and the like. Or, terrible — fear-inducing for the wicked...

body.text: lajjayā mandahasitam ālakṣyāha-rajany eṣeti ||BhPC_10,29.19||
body.translated_text: Perceiving their bashful gentle smiles, he says — '<s>rajany eṣā</s>' etc. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.19 ||

children.text: mātaraḥ pitaraḥ putrā bhrātaraḥ patayaś ca vaḥ /
children.translated_text: Your mothers, fathers, sons, brothers, and husbands

children.text: vicinvanti hy apaśyanto mā kṛḍhvaṃ bandhusādhvasam //
children.translated_text: are searching for you, not seeing [you]. Do not cause anxiety to your relatives! //

body.text: kiṃ ca mātara iti | vicinvanti mṛgayante | bandhūnāṃ sādhvasaṃ kṛcchraṃ mā kṛdhvaṃ mā kurutety arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.20||
body.translated_text: Moreover — '<s>mātaraḥ</s>' etc. | '<s>Vicinvanti</s>' means they search. | '<s>Bandhusādhvasam</s>' — do not cause (<s>mā kṛdhvam</s>, i.e., do not do) distress (<s>sādhvasam</s>, i.e., <s>kṛcchram</s>) to relatives (<s>bandhūnām</s>) — this is the meaning. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.20 ||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.21
dṛṣṭaṃ vanaṃ kusumitaṃ rākeśakararañjitam / yamunānilalīlaijat tarupallavaśobhitam //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.21 — You have seen the forest in bloom, beautified by the rays of the full moon, adorned with tree-leaves trembling in the playful breeze from the <s>Yamunā</s>. //

body.text: īṣatpraṇayakopenānyato vilokayantī pratyāha-dṛṣṭam iti | rākeśasya pūrṇacandrasya karai rañjitam | yamunāsparśino 'nilasya līlā mandagatis tayā ejantaḥ kampamānās tarūṇāṃ pallavās taiḥ śobhitam ||BhPC_10,29.21||
body.translated_text: Looking away with slight amorous anger, she responds — '<s>dṛṣṭam</s>' etc. | '<s>Rākeśasya</s>' means the full moon; '<s>karaiḥ</s>' means beautified by its rays. | '<s>Yamunā</s>-touching wind's <s>līlā</s>' means its gentle movement; by that the trembling leaves and sprouts are adorned...

children.text: tad yāta mā ciraṃ goṣṭhaṃ śuśrūṣadhvaṃ patīn satīḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore go, do not tarry, return to the cow-settlement! Serve your husbands, O faithful women!

children.text: krandanti vatsā bālāś ca tān pāyayata duhyata //
children.translated_text: The calves and children are crying — feed them and milk [the cows]! //

body.text: satīḥ he satyaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.22||
body.translated_text: '<s>Satīḥ</s>' — O truthful ones! || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.22 ||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.23
atha vā madabhisnehād bhavatyo yantritāśayāḥ / āgatā hy upapannaṃ vaḥ prīyante mayi jantavaḥ //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.23 — Or perhaps, out of love for me, you have come with hearts captivated — that is fitting for you, for all creatures are devoted to me. //

body.text: saṃrambhakṣubhitadṛṣṭīḥ pratyāha-athaveti | yantritāśayā vaśīkṛtacittāḥ | upapannaṃ yuktam | prīyante prītā bhavanti ||BhPC_10,29.23||
body.translated_text: He addresses those whose gazes are agitated with indignation — '<s>athavā</s>' etc. | '<s>Yantritāśayāḥ</s>' means those whose minds are captivated. | '<s>Upapannam</s>' means appropriate. | '<s>Prīyante</s>' means they become devoted. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.23 ||

children.text: bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ paro dharmo hy amāyayā /
children.translated_text: The highest duty of women is devoted service to the husband, without deceit,
and the welfare of his relatives, O auspicious ones, and the nourishment of their offspring. //

body.text: dṛṣṭādṛṣṭabhayapradarśanena nivartayati-bhartur ity ādi ślokatrayeṇa ||BhPC_10,29.24|| ||BhPC_10,29.25||
body.translated_text: He discourages them by showing both visible and invisible dangers — '<s>bhartuḥ</s>' etc., in these three verses. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.24 || || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.25 ||

children.text: asvargyam ayaśasyaṃ ca phalgu kṛcchraṃ bhayāvaham /
children.translated_text: Adultery of a woman of good family brings no heaven, brings infamy,
is trifling, painful, fear-inducing, and is despised everywhere. //

body.text: phalgu tuccham | kṛcchraṃ duḥsaṃpādyam | aupapattyaṃ jārasaukhyam ||BhPC_10,29.26||
body.translated_text: '<s>Phalgu</s>' means worthless. | '<s>Kṛcchram</s>' means difficult to achieve. | '<s>Aupapatyam</s>' means the pleasure of a paramour. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.26 ||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.27
śravaṇād darśanād dhyānān mayi bhāvo 'nukīrtanāt / na tathā sannikarṣeṇa pratiyāta tato gṛhān //
body.translated_text: <s>BhP</s> 10.29.27 — Through hearing, seeing, meditating on me, and through recounting [my deeds], devotion arises — not so much through physical proximity. Therefore return to your homes! //

body.text: kiṃ ca śravaṇād iti ||BhPC_10,29.27|| ||BhPC_10,29.28||
body.translated_text: Moreover — '<s>śravaṇāt</s>' etc. || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.27 || || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.28 ||

children.text: kṛtvā mukhāny ava śucaḥ śvasanena śuṣyad bimbādharāṇi caraṇena bhuvaḥ likhantyaḥ /
children.translated_text: Lowering their faces, drying their berry-red lips with sighs of sorrow,

children.text: asrair upāttamaṣibhiḥ kucakuṅkumāni tasthur mṛjantya uruduḥkhabharāḥ sma tūṣṇīm //
children.translated_text: scratching the ground with their toes, wiping with tears the saffron-marks on their breasts stained with collyrium — they stood in silence, bearing a great weight of grief. //

body.text: cintāṃ prāptānāṃ sthitim āha-kṛtveti | śucaḥ śokād udgatena śvasanena śuṣyanto bimbaphalasadṛśā adharā yeṣu mukheṣu tāni ava avāñci kṛtvā tathā 'ṅguṣṭhena mahīṃ likhantyaḥ | tathā gṛhītakajjalair aśrubhiḥ kucakuṅkumāni kṣalayantyas tūṣṇīṃ sthitāḥ | yata uruduḥkhasya bharo bhāro yāsāṃ tāḥ ||BhPC_10,29.29||
body.translated_text: He describes the state of those who had fallen into deep thought — '<s>kṛtvā</s>' etc. | '<s>Śucaḥ</s>' — with breath exhaled from grief, the lips resembling <s>bimba</s> fruits dry; lowering the faces in which these [lips] are, and also with the toes...

children.text: preṣṭhaṃ priyetaram iva pratibhāṣamāṇaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tadarthavinivartitasarvakāmāḥ /
children.translated_text: To <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who spoke to [them who were] most beloved as though to [mere] acquaintances — they who had abandoned all desires for his sake,

children.text: netre vimṛjya ruditopahate sma kiñcit saṃrambhagadgadagiro 'bruvatānuraktāḥ //
children.translated_text: wiping their tear-stained eyes, with voices choked with indignation, the devoted ones spoke somewhat: //

body.text: kiṃ ca preṣṭham iti | kiñcit saṃrambhena kopāveśena gadgadā giro yāsāṃ tā abruvat sma | saṃrambhe kāraṇaṃ-preṣṭham ity ādi | priyetaram iva pratibhāṣamāṇaṃ pratyācakṣāṇam ||BhPC_10,29.30||
body.translated_text: Moreover — '<s>preṣṭham</s>' etc. | '<s>Kiñcit</s>' — with voices choked (<s>gadgadāḥ</s>) by indignation (<s>saṃrambheṇa</s>), i.e., by the onset of anger, they spoke. | The cause of the indignation — '<s>preṣṭham</s>' etc. | He spoke to [them who were] most beloved as though to mere acquaintances...

children.translated_text: The <s>Gopīs</s> spoke:

children.text: maivaṃ vibho 'rhati bhavān gadituṃ nṛśaṃsaṃ santyajya sarvaviṣayāṃs tava pādamūlam /
children.translated_text: O Lord, you should not speak such cruel [words]! Having abandoned all worldly objects for the sake of your lotus feet,

children.text: bhaktā bhajasva duravagraha mā tyajāsmān devo yathādipuruṣo bhajate mumukṣūn //
children.translated_text: O devoted ones, worship us who have served you! O hard-to-grasp one, do not forsake us — just as God, the primal <s>Puruṣa</s>, accepts those who seek liberation! //

body.text: nṛśaṃsaṃ krūram | he duravagraha svacchanda, tava pādamūlaṃ bhaktāḥ sevitavatīr asmān bhajasva mā tyajeti ||BhPC_10,29.31||
body.translated_text: '<s>Nṛśaṃsam</s>' means cruel. | O '<s>duravagraha</s>' — O self-willed one, accept us who have served (<s>bhaktāḥ</s>) your lotus feet (<s>pādamūlam</s>); do not forsake [us]! || <s>BhPC</s> 10.29.31 ||

children.text: yat patyapatyasuhṛdām anuvṛttir aṅga strīṇāṃ svadharma iti dharmavidā tvayoktam /
children.translated_text: That the duty (<s>dharma</s>) of women, O dear one, is devotion to husband, offspring, and friends — thus you, the knower of <s>dharma</s>, have said.

children.text: astv evam etad upadeśapade tvayīśe preṣṭho bhavāṃs tanubhṛtāṃ kila bandhur[*14] ātmā //
children.translated_text: Let this be so, but may this instruction be directed toward you, O Lord — for you, dear one, are indeed the kinsman and the very self of all embodied beings! //

body.text: [*14] bandhuro manohara ātmā yasyeti vā |
body.translated_text: [*14] Or, '<s>bandhuraḥ</s>' means charming, and '<s>ātmā</s>' means [their very] self. |

body.text: api ca yad uktam "patyapatya-" ity ādi tvayā dharmavideti sopahāsam evam, etad upadeśānāṃ pade viṣaye tvayy evāstu | upadeśapadatve hetuḥ-īśa iti | vividiṣāvākyena sarvopadeśānām īśaparatvāvagamād iti bhāvaḥ | īśatve hetuḥ-ātmā kila bhavān iti | bhogyasya hi sarvasya bhoktā ātmaiveśa ity ataḥ preṣṭho bandhuś ca bhavān eveti sarvabandhuṣu karaṇīyaṃ tvayy evāstv ity arthaḥ | atha vā dharmopadeśānāṃ pade sthāne dharmopadeṣṭari tvayi saty asmāsu ca dharmaṃ jijñāsamānāsu satīṣu tvayā dharmavidā yad uktam evam etad astu | na tu tvaṃ dharmopadeṣṭā kintu bhavān ātmeti | atha vā yad uktam etad upadeśapade tadgocare puruṣe 'stu nāma, tvayi tu īśe svāmini saty evam | kā kvā naivam ity arthaḥ | yatas tanubhṛtāṃ tvam ātmā phalarūpa iti | yadvā yad uktaṃ "patyādiśuśrūṣaṇaṃ dharma" iti evam etat tvayy evāstu | kutaḥ | upadeśapade śuśrūṣaṇīyatvenopadiśyamānānāṃ patyādīnāṃ pade 'dhiṣṭhāne | kutaḥ īśe | na hīśvaram adhiṣṭhānaṃ vinā ko 'pi patiputrādir nāmeti | anyat samānam | alam ativistareṇa ||BhPC_10,29.32||
body.translated_text: Moreover, what was said — '<s>patyapatya-</s>' etc. — by you as a knower of <s>dharma</s>, [this is said] mockingly (<s>sopahāsam</s>); let this be so regarding you yourself, who are the object (<s>pade</s>, in the domain) of [all] instructions (<s>upadeśānām</s>). | The reason for being the object of instruction — '<s>Īśa</s>' (Lord). | The commentary elaborates further...

children.text: kurvanti hi tvayi ratiṃ kuśalāḥ sva ātman[*15] nityapriye patisutādibhir ārtidaiḥ kim /
children.translated_text: The wise indeed direct their love toward you, the self, the eternally beloved — what use are husbands, sons, and others who only bring suffering?

children.text: tan naḥ prasīda parameśvara[*16] mā sma chindyā[*17] āśāṃ bhṛtāṃ tvayi cirād aravindanetra //
children.translated_text: Therefore be pleased with us, O Supreme Lord! Do not sever the hope that has been cherished in you for so long, O lotus-eyed one! //

body.text:
[*15] ātman ātmani |
[*16] "varadeśvara" iti pāṭhaḥ |
[*17] "chindyādāśām" iti pāṭhaḥ | tatra bhavān ity adhyāhāraḥ, chāndasaḥ puruṣavyatyayo vā |
body.translated_text: [*15] '<s>Ātman</s>' means in the self. | [*16] The reading '<s>varadeśvara</s>' [is also found]. | [*17] The reading '<s>chindyād āśām</s>' [is also found]. | There '<s>bhavān</s>' is to be supplied; or the change of person is Vedic license. |

body.text: etat sadācāreṇa draḍhayantyaḥ prārthayante-kurvantīti | kuśalāḥ śāstranipuṇāḥ | tathā ca śāstram-"kiṃ prajayā kariṣyāmo yeṣāṃ no 'yam ātmā 'yaṃ ca lokaḥ" iti ||BhPC_10,29.33||
body.translated_text: This they confirm through virtuous conduct and beseech [Him] — they do [so]. ‘Skilled’ means learned in the scriptures. And the scripture [states]: ‘What shall we do with progeny, we for whom this Self is [all] and this world [is ours]?’ ||BhPC_10,29.33||

children.text: cittaṃ sukhena bhavatāpahṛtaṃ gṛheṣu yan nirviśaty uta karāv api gṛhyakṛtye /
children.translated_text: Our mind, [previously] happily entering into household affairs, has been stolen by You; / and our hands too [that were engaged] in domestic tasks,

children.text: pādau padaṃ na calatas tava pādamūlād yāmaḥ kathaṃ vrajam atho karavāma kiṃ vā //
children.translated_text: our feet do not move a step from the base of Your feet. / How shall we go to <s>Vraja</s>? And what shall we do? //

body.text: kiṃ ca "pratiyāta" iti yad uktaṃ tad aśakyaṃ, tvayaiva cittādīnām apahṛtatvād ity āhuḥ-cittam iti | yad asmākaṃ cittam etāvantaṃ kālaṃ sukhena gṛheṣu nirviśati tat tvayāpahṛtam | karāv api yau gṛhakṛtye nirviśatas tāv api | sukhātmanā tvayeti vā ||BhPC_10,29.34||
body.translated_text: Moreover, the statement ‘Go back’ is impossible, since mind and the rest have been stolen by You Yourself — thus they say with ‘cittam’ (mind). That mind of ours which for all this time happily entered into household affairs — that has been stolen by You. And the hands too that were engaged in domestic tasks — they too. ‘By You who are the very nature of bliss’ — or [alternatively] thus. ||BhPC_10,29.34||

children.translated_text: O dear one, sprinkle upon us — with the nectar-flood of Your lower lip, / with laughter, glances, and melodious song — the fire born in our hearts.

children.text: no ced vayaṃ virahajāgnyupayuktadehā dhyānena yāma padayoḥ padavīṃ sakhe te //
children.translated_text: If not, we, with bodies consumed by the fire of separation, / shall reach the path of Your feet through meditation, O friend. //

body.text: ato 'ṅga he kṛṣṇa, no 'smākaṃ tavādharāmṛtapūrvakeṇa tavaiva hāsasahitenāvalokena kalagītena ca jāto yo hṛcchayāgniḥ kāmāgnis taṃ siñca | no ced vayaṃ tāvad eko 'gnis tathā virahāj janiṣyate yo 'gnis tena copayuktadehā dagdhaśarīrā yogina iva te padavīm antikaṃ dhyānena yāma prāpnuyāmaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.35||
body.translated_text: Therefore, O dear one, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, sprinkle the fire of desire (<s>kāmāgni</s>) born in our hearts — that fire born through Your laughter combined with glances and melodious song, preceded by the nectar of Your lips. If not, then indeed one fire [burns already], and another fire will be born from separation; with bodies consumed by that fire, like yogins, we shall reach Your proximity through meditation. ||BhPC_10,29.35||

children.text: yarhy ambujākṣa tava pādatalaṃ ramāyā dattakṣaṇaṃ kvacid araṇyajanapriyasya /
children.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one, since that time when [we] touched the sole of Your foot, / which even <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) receives only on occasion — [the foot] of You who are dear to the forest-dwellers —

children.text: asprākṣma tatprabhṛti nānyasamakṣam aṅga sthātuṃs tvayābhiramitā bata pārayāmaḥ //
children.translated_text: from that time onward, O dear one, we who have been delighted by You / cannot bear to stand in the presence of another. //

body.text: nanu svapatīn evopagacchata ta enam agniṃ siñceyur iti cet tatrāhuḥ-yarhīti | ramāyā lakṣmyā dattakṣaṇaṃ dattotsavaṃ dattāvasaraṃ vā | tad api kvacid eva na sarvadā | araṇyajanāḥ priyā yasya tasya tava | araṇyajanapriyatvād araṇye kvacid yarhy asprākṣma spṛṣṭavatyo vayaṃ tatra ca tvayābhiramitā ānanditāḥ satyas tadārabhyānyasamakṣaṃ sthātum api na pārayāmaḥ | tucchās te na rocanta ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.36||
body.translated_text: Now if [it be said] ‘Go to your own husbands; they can sprinkle this fire’ — to that they reply with ‘yarhi.’ ‘Of <s>Ramā</s>’ means <s>Lakṣmī</s>; ‘given the occasion’ means given the festival or given the opportunity. And even that only sometimes, not always. ‘Of You, to whom the forest-dwellers are dear.’ Because of His love for the forest people, somewhere in the forest, when we touched [His feet] and were delighted by You — made joyful — from then onward we cannot bear to stand even in the presence of another. The meaning is: they are insignificant and do not please us. ||BhPC_10,29.36||

children.text: śrīr yat padāmbujarajaś cakame tulasyā labdhvāpi vakṣasi padaṃ kila bhṛtyajuṣṭam /
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), who has obtained a place on [Your] chest — a place served by [Your] attendants — / yet desires the dust of Your lotus feet along with <s>Tulasī</s>.

children.text: yasyāḥ svavīkṣaṇakṛte 'nyasuraprayāsas tadvad vayaṃ ca tava pādarajaḥ prapannāḥ //
children.translated_text: She, for whose mere glance other gods exert great effort — / we too, like her, have taken refuge in the dust of Your feet. //

body.text: tvatpādasaubhāgyaṃ tv aticitram ity āhuḥ-śrīr iti | vakṣasy asāpatnyaṃ sthānaṃ labdhvāpi tulasyā sapatnyā saha tava pādāmbujarajaḥ kāmayate sma | bhṛtyaiḥ sarvair juṣṭam iti saubhāgyātirekoktiḥ | yasyāḥ svavīkṣaṇakṛte śrīr ātmānaṃ vilokaya tv ity etad artham anyeṣāṃ brahmādīnāṃ tapobhiḥ prayāsaḥ sā tad rajas tadvad vayam api prapannā iti ||BhPC_10,29.37||
body.translated_text: The good fortune of Your feet is utterly amazing — thus they say with ‘<s>Śrī</s>.’ Having obtained on [His] chest a position without a co-wife, even so she desires the dust of His lotus feet together with <s>Tulasī</s> as a co-wife. ‘Served by all attendants’ — this is a statement of surpassing good fortune. For whose self-glance — meaning ‘Look upon me!’ — for this purpose the effort of other gods such as <s>Brahmā</s> through austerities — she [desires] that dust; likewise we too have taken refuge. ||BhPC_10,29.37||

children.text: tan naḥ prasīda vṛjinārdana te 'nghrimūlaṃ prāptā visṛjya vasatīs tvadupāsanāśāḥ /
children.translated_text: Therefore be pleased with us, O destroyer of afflictions; we have reached the base of Your feet, / having abandoned our homes, with our hopes set on worshipping You.
Grant servitude to us, whose souls are scorched by the intense desire / [aroused by] Your beautiful smile and glance, O jewel among men. //

body.text: he vṛjinārdana[*18] duḥkhahantaḥ, tvadupāsane tvadbhajana evāśā yāsāṃ tā vayaṃ vāsatīr gṛhān visṛjya hitvā yogina iva prāptāḥ | tava sundarasmitavilasitanirīkṣaṇena yas tīvraḥ kāmas tena taptacittānām | he puruṣaratna, dāsyaṃ dehi ||BhPC_10,29.38||
body.translated_text: O destroyer of afflictions (<s>vṛjinārdana</s>)[*18], O remover of suffering! We whose hope is solely in Your worship, in Your devotion, having abandoned our dwellings, having left our homes like yogins, have arrived. With souls scorched by the intense desire [aroused by] the play of Your beautiful smile and glance — O jewel among men, grant us servitude! ||BhPC_10,29.38||

children.translated_text: Seeing Your face covered with locks of hair, [adorned with] the beauty of earrings on the cheeks, / the nectar of the lower lip, the smiling glance,

children.text: dattābhayaṃ ca bhujadaṇḍayugaṃ vilokya vakṣaḥ śriyaikaramaṇaṃ[*19] ca bhavāma[*20] dāsyaḥ //
children.translated_text: and the pair of arm-pillars that grant fearlessness, / and the chest that is the sole delight of <s>Śrī</s>[*19] — we become[*20] Your maidservants. //

body.text:
[*18] niṣedhapakṣe vṛjinārda na iti cchedaḥ, gṛhādi tyaktvā na prāptā vayam iti yojanā |
[*19] śriyāḥ ekaramaṇam iti cchedaḥ | sandhir ārṣaḥ |
[*20] niṣedhapakṣe kiṃ dāsyo bhavāmeti kākvā naivety arthaḥ |
body.translated_text:
[*18] In the negative interpretation, the word-division is ‘vṛjina-arda-na,’ [meaning] ‘we have not arrived having abandoned our homes’ — this is the construction.
[*19] The word-division is ‘śriyāḥ ekaramaṇam.’ The sandhi is Vedic.
[*20] In the negative interpretation, [the meaning is] ‘Shall we become maidservants?’ — the rhetorical question implies ‘certainly not.’

body.text: nanu gṛhasvāmyaṃ vihāya dāsyaṃ kim iti prārthyate 'ta āhuḥ-vīkṣyati | alakāvṛtamukhaṃ keśāntarair āvṛtamukham | tathā kuṇḍalayoḥ śrīr yayos te gaṇḍasthale yasmin, adhare sudhā yasmiṃs tac ca tac ca tava mukhaṃ vīkṣya dattābhayaṃ bhujadaṇḍayugmaṃ vakṣaś ca śriyā ekam eva ramaṇaṃ ratijanakaṃ vīkṣya dāsya eva bhavāmeti ||BhPC_10,29.39||
body.translated_text: Now why is servitude sought after abandoning the sovereignty of the household? To that they reply with ‘vīkṣya.’ ‘Face covered with locks of hair’ — face covered between the strands of hair. And the beauty of the two earrings on the cheek-surface on which, and the nectar on the lower lip on which — that face, having seen it; and having seen the pair of arm-pillars that grant fearlessness, and the chest that is the sole cause of delight for <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — we become nothing but maidservants. ||BhPC_10,29.39||

children.text: kā stry aṅga te kalapadāyatamūrcchitena[*21] sammohitāryacaritān na[*22] calet trilokyām /
children.translated_text: What woman, O dear one, in the three worlds would not swerve from noble conduct, / being enchanted by Your melodious, extended, modulated[*21] [flute-song]?

children.text: trailokyasaubhagam idaṃ ca nirīkṣya rūpaṃ yad godvijadrumamṛgāḥ pulakāny abibhran //
children.translated_text: Seeing this form that is the beauty of the three worlds, / even cows, birds, trees, and deer bore horripilation! //

body.text:
[*21] "padāyataveṇugītasaṃmohitā" iti pāṭhaḥ |
[*22] niṣedhapakṣe āryacaritabhaṅgabhiyā kā strī nāpayāyād iti yojanā |
body.translated_text:
[*21] Alternative reading: ‘enchanted by the flute-song of melodious, extended notes.’
[*22] In the negative interpretation, the construction is: ‘Which woman, out of fear of transgressing noble conduct, would not go away?’

body.text: nanu jugupsitam aupapatyam ity uktam, tatrāhuḥ-kā strīti | aṅga he kṛṣṇa, kalāni padāni yasmiṃs tad āyataṃ dhīrgaṃ mūrcchitaṃ svarālāpabhedas tena | pāṭhāntare[*23] kalapadāmṛtamayaṃ veṇugītaṃ tena saṃmohitā kā vā strī āryacaritān nijadharmān na calet | yanmohitāḥ puruṣā api calitāḥ, kiṃ ca trailokyasaubhagam iti yad yataḥ abibhrann abibharuḥ | tvaddyotakaśabdaśravaṇa-mātreṇāpi tāvan nijadharmatyāgo yuktaḥ, kiṃ punas tvadanubhaveneti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_10,29.40||
body.translated_text: Now it was said that paramour-love is despicable — to that they reply with ‘kā strī.’ O dear one, O <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by that which is melodious, extended, long, and modulated — modulation being the varieties of musical elaboration — by that [song]; in the alternative reading[*23], by the flute-song filled with the nectar of melodious notes — what woman, thus enchanted, would not swerve from noble conduct, from her own duties? Since even men, being enchanted [by Him], have swerved. Moreover, ‘the beauty of the three worlds’ — since (‘yat’ = ‘because’) they bore, they experienced [horripilation]. Even by merely hearing the word that reveals You, the abandonment of one’s own duty is fitting — how much more so through direct experience of You! This is the purport. ||BhPC_10,29.40||

body.text: [*23] kalapadāmṛtaveṇugītasaṃmohitety evaṃrūpe |
body.translated_text: [*23] The alternative reading has the form: kalapadāmṛtaveṇugītasaṃmohita.

children.text: vyaktaṃ bhavān vrajabhayārtiharo[*24] 'bhijāto devo yathādipuruṣaḥ suralokagoptā /
children.translated_text: Clearly You have been born[*24] as the very god, like the primeval <s>Puruṣa</s>, / the protector of the world of the gods, for removing the fear and suffering of <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text: tan no[*25] nidhehi karapaṅkajam ārtabandho taptastaneṣu ca śirassu ca kiṅkarīṇām //
children.translated_text: Therefore, O friend of the afflicted, place Your lotus hand / upon the burning breasts and heads of Your maidservants.[*25] //

body.text:
[*24] "vrajajanārtiharaḥ" iti pāṭhaḥ |
[*25] niṣedhapakṣe kiṅkarīṇām api śirassu karaṃ no vidhehi mā sthāpayeti |
body.translated_text:
[*24] Alternative reading: ‘remover of the suffering of the people of <s>Vraja</s>.’
[*25] In the negative interpretation: ‘Do not place Your hand upon the heads of Your maidservants.’

body.text: vyaktaṃ niścitam ||BhPC_10,29.41||
body.translated_text: ‘Clearly’ means certainly. ||BhPC_10,29.41||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.42
śrīśuka uvāca
iti viklavitaṃ tāsāṃ śrutvā yogeśvareśvaraḥ / prahasya sadayaṃ gopīr ātmārāmo 'py arīramat //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,29.42
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
Having heard this distraught speech of theirs, the lord of the lords of <s>yoga</s>, / smiling compassionately, delighted the <s>gopīs</s>, though He is self-delighted (<s>ātmārāma</s>). //

body.text: viklavitaṃ pāravaśyapralapitam | gopīḥ arīramad ramayāmāsa ||BhPC_10,29.42||
body.translated_text: ‘Distraught speech’ means speech uttered in helplessness. He delighted, He caused delight to, the <s>gopīs</s>. ||BhPC_10,29.42||

children.translated_text: <s>Acyuta</s>, surrounded by those [<s>gopīs</s>] who had assembled, whose actions were noble, / whose faces had blossomed through the glance of the beloved,
with the radiance of His teeth [shining] in His generous smile like <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) blossoms, / shone like the moon (<s>eṇāṅka</s>) surrounded by stars. //

body.text: priyasyekṣaṇenotphullāni mukhāni yāsāṃ tābhiḥ udārahāsaś ca dvijāś ca teṣu kundakusumavad-dīdhitir yasya saḥ | eṇāṅkaś candraḥ ||BhPC_10,29.43|| ||BhPC_10,29.44|| ||BhPC_10,29.45||
body.translated_text: [Those] whose faces had blossomed through the glance of the beloved — with those [<s>gopīs</s>]; with generous smile, and teeth, and among them the radiance like that of <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) flowers. <s>Eṇāṅka</s> means the moon. ||BhPC_10,29.43|| ||BhPC_10,29.44|| ||BhPC_10,29.45||

children.translated_text: With the extension of arms, embraces, the touching of hands, locks of hair, / girdles, and breasts, with playful nail-tip scratches,

children.text: kṣvelyāvalokahasitair vrajasundarīṇām uttambhayan ratipatiṃ ramayāṃ cakāra //
children.translated_text: with sportive glances and laughter, arousing <s>Ratipati</s> (the lord of love, <s>Kāma</s>) / in the beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>, He made love to them. //

body.text: bāhuprasāraś ca parirambhaś ca karādīnām ālabhanaṃ sparśaś ca narma parihāsaś ca nakhāgrapātaś ca taiḥ | kṣvelyā krīḍayā | avalokaiś ca hastitaiś ca kāmaṃ tāsām uddīpayaṃs tā ramayāmāsa ||BhPC_10,29.46||
body.translated_text: Extension of arms, and embraces, and the touching of hands and the rest, and play meaning jest, and the falling of nail-tips — with those. Through sport, through glances, and through laughter — kindling their desire, He delighted them. ||BhPC_10,29.46||

children.translated_text: Thus having received honor from <s>Bhagavān Kṛṣṇa</s>, the great-souled one,
those proud women considered themselves / the most exalted among all women on earth. //

body.text: mahātmano vimuktacittāt ||BhPC_10,29.47||
body.translated_text: ‘Great-souled’ means one whose mind is free [from attachment]. ||BhPC_10,29.47||

body.text:
BhP_10,29.48
tāsāṃ tatsaubhagamadaṃ vīkṣya mānaṃ ca keśavaḥ / praśamāya prasādāya tatraivāntaradhīyata //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,29.48
Seeing their pride, the intoxication of that good fortune, and arrogance, / <s>Keśava</s>, for the purpose of calming and gracing [them], disappeared right there. //

body.text: tatsaubhagena madam asvādhīnatām | mānaṃ garvaṃ | keśavaḥ kaś ca īśaś ca tau vaśayatīti tathā saḥ ||BhPC_10,29.48||
body.translated_text: Through that good fortune, intoxication meaning loss of self-control; arrogance meaning pride. <s>Keśava</s>: ‘Ka’ (= <s>Brahmā</s>) and ‘Īśa’ (= <s>Śiva</s>) — He who brings them under His control, thus He is called so. ||BhPC_10,29.48||

body.text: iti śrīmadbhāgavate mahāpurāṇe daśamaskandhe pūrvārdhe bhāvārthadīpikāyāṃ ṭīkāyāṃ ekonatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ **29**
body.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the tenth book, first half, in the commentary called <s>Bhāvārthadīpikā</s>, the twenty-ninth chapter. **29**

children.translated_text: [Chapter 30:] The search for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> by the <s>gopīs</s> burning with the anguish of separation,

children.text: unamattavan na niyataṃ bhramantībhir vane vane // 1 //
children.translated_text: wandering like madwomen, unrestrained, from forest to forest. // 1 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.01
śrīśuka uvāca
antarhite bhagavati sahasaiva vrajāṅganāḥ / atapyaṃs tam acakṣāṇāḥ kariṇya iva yūthapam //
body.translated_text:
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
When the <s>Bhagavān</s> suddenly disappeared, the women of <s>Vraja</s>, not seeing Him, were distressed — like female elephants [separated] from the leader of the herd.

body.text: acakṣāṇā apaśyantyaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.1||
body.translated_text: 'Not seeing' (<s>acakṣāṇāḥ</s>) means 'not perceiving.'

children.translated_text: By His gait, loving smiles, playful glances, charming speech, and the diversions of His play,

children.text: ākṣiptacittāḥ pramadā ramāpates tās tā viceṣṭā jagṛhus tadātmikāḥ //
children.translated_text: the young women, their minds captivated by the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), assumed His very gestures, becoming one with Him.

body.text: gatyā cānurāgasmitābhyāṃ vibhramekṣitāni savilāsanirīkṣaṇāni taiś ca manoramā ālāpāś ca vihārāḥ krīḍāś ca vibhramā anye ca vilāsās taiś ca ramāpater gatyādibhir etair ākṣiptāny ākṛṣṭāni cittāni yāsāṃ tāḥ, atas tasminn evātmā yāsāṃ tās tasya vividhāś ceṣṭhā jagṛhus tadanukaraṇenākrīḍan ||BhPC_10,30.2||
body.translated_text: By His gait, loving smiles, playful glances — that is, glances accompanied by coquetry — by these, and by charming conversation, diversions — that is, sports — and other playful gestures of the Lord of <s>Ramā</s>, those whose minds were drawn — that is, attracted — by His gait and the like; hence, those whose very self was in Him alone — they assumed His various [gestures].

children.translated_text: In His gait, smile, glances, speech, and the like, the beloved ones, with forms possessed by their beloved,

children.text: asāv ahaṃ tv ity abalās tadātmikā nyavediṣuḥ kṛṣṇavihāravibhramāḥ //
children.translated_text: declared to one another, 'This one is I!' — those women, being one with Him, enacting <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s playful diversions.

body.text: api ca gatismiteti | priyasya gatyādiṣu pratirūḍhā āviṣṭā mūrtayo yāsāṃ tāḥ | ataḥ kṛṣṇavihāra-vibhramāḥ kṛṣṇasya eva vihāravibhramāḥ krīḍāvilāsā yāsāṃ tāḥ | aham eva kṛṣṇa iti parasparaṃ niveditavatyaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.3||
body.translated_text: Moreover, [the verse] 'in His gait, smile...' — those whose bodies were possessed, that is, entered into, by the beloved's gait and the like. Hence, '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s playful diversions' means those whose playful sports were those of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself. 'I am <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!' — thus they declared to one another.

children.text: gāyantya uccair amum eva saṃhatā vicikyur unmattakavad vanād vanam /
children.translated_text: Singing aloud about Him alone, they searched together like madwomen, from forest to forest;

children.text: papracchur ākāśavad antaraṃ bahir bhūteṣu santaṃ puruṣaṃ vanaspatīn //
children.translated_text: they asked the trees about the <s>Puruṣa</s> (Supreme Person) who dwells within and without all beings, as [He pervades] space.

body.text: kiṃ ca gāyantya iti | vanād vanāntaraṃ gacchantyo vicikyur amṛgayan | unmattatulyatvam āha- vanaspatīn papracchuḥ | bhūteṣv antaraṃ madhye santaṃ puruṣaṃ bahiś ca santam iti ||BhPC_10,30.4||
body.translated_text: Moreover, [the verse] 'singing...' — going from one forest to another, they searched, that is, they sought. Their being like madwomen is shown — they asked the trees. [They asked about] the <s>Puruṣa</s> dwelling in the midst of all beings, and also existing outside [them].

children.text: dṛṣṭo vaḥ kaccid aśvattha plakṣa nyagrodha no manaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Have you seen, O <s>Aśvattha</s> (fig tree), O <s>Plakṣa</s> (wavy-leaf fig), O <s>Nyagrodha</s> (banyan) — [He who stole] our minds
the son of <s>Nanda</s>, who departed, having stolen [our hearts] with His loving smiles and glances?'

body.text: tat prapañcayati navabhiḥ-tatra mahattvād ete paśyeyur ity āśayāśvatthādīn pṛcchanti-dṛṣṭa iti | premahāsavilasitair avalokanair asmākaṃ mano hṛtvā cora iva gato vo yuṣmābhiḥ kiṃ dṛṣṭa iti ||BhPC_10,30.5||
body.translated_text: He elaborates this in nine [verses]. There, thinking that because of their greatness these [trees] might have seen [Him], they ask the <s>aśvattha</s> and other [trees]: 'Have you seen [Him]?' — [He who,] having stolen our minds with [His] loving, sportive smiles and glances, has gone like a thief — has He been seen by you?

children.text: kaccit kurabakāśokanāgapunnāgacampakāḥ / rāmānujo māninīnām ito[*26] darpaharasmitaḥ //
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Kurabaka</s>, <s>Aśoka</s>, <s>Nāga</s>, <s>Punnāga</s>, <s>Campaka</s> — has the younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, whose smile steals the pride of haughty women, [passed] this way?'

body.text: [*26] "gataḥ" iti pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: An alternate reading is '<s>gataḥ</s>' (gone).

body.text: mahāntaḥ svapuṣpair bahūpakāriṇaś ceti kurabakādīn pṛcchanti-kaccid iti | he kurabakādayaḥ, darpaharaṃ smitaṃ yasya saḥ ito gataḥ kaccid dṛṣṭa iti ||BhPC_10,30.6||
body.translated_text: Being great and very beneficial through their flowers, they ask the <s>Kurabaka</s> and others: 'Have you seen?' — O <s>Kurabaka</s> and others, [He] whose smile steals pride — has He gone from here? Has He been seen?

body.text:
BhP_10,30.07
kaccit tulasi kalyāṇi govindacaraṇapriye / saha tvālikulair bibhrad dṛṣṭas te 'tipriyo 'cyutaḥ //
body.translated_text:
<s>BhP</s> 10.30.07
'O <s>Tulasī</s>, auspicious one, dear to the feet of <s>Govinda</s>, has <s>Acyuta</s>, wearing you together with swarms of bees, your dearest, been seen by you?'

body.text: alikulaiḥ saha tvā tvāṃ bibhrat tavātipriyas tvayā kiṃ dṛṣṭa iti ||BhPC_10,30.7||
body.translated_text: 'Wearing you together with swarms of bees' — [meaning] carrying you (<s>tvā</s>); your dearest one — has He been seen by you?

body.text:
BhP_10,30.08
mālaty adarśi vaḥ kaccin mallike jātiyūthike / prītiṃ vo janayan yātaḥ karasparśena mādhavaḥ //
body.translated_text:
<s>BhP</s> 10.30.08
'O <s>Mālatī</s>, has He been seen? And you, <s>Mallikā</s>, <s>Jātī</s>, <s>Yūthikā</s> — has <s>Mādhava</s> passed by, generating delight in you by the touch of His hand?'

body.text: guṇātireke 'pi namratvād imāḥ paśyeyur iti pṛcchanti-mālatīti | he mālati mallike, jāti, yūthike, vo yuṣmābhiḥ kim adarśi dṛṣṭaḥ | karasparśena vaḥ prītiṃ janayan kiṃ yāta iti | atra mālatījātyor avāntaraviśeṣo draṣṭavyaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.8||
body.translated_text: Even though surpassing in qualities, because of their humility, [the <s>gopīs</s> think] these [flowers] might have seen Him, and ask: 'O <s>Mālatī</s>, <s>Mallikā</s>, <s>Jātī</s>, <s>Yūthikā</s> — has He been seen by you? Generating delight in you by the touch of His hand — has He gone?' Here, a subordinate specific difference between <s>Mālatī</s> and <s>Jātī</s> should be noted.

children.translated_text: 'O <s>Cūta</s> (mango), <s>Priyāla</s>, <s>Panasa</s> (jackfruit), <s>Āsana</s>, <s>Kovidāra</s>, <s>Jambū</s> (rose-apple), <s>Arka</s>, <s>Bilva</s> (wood-apple), <s>Bakula</s>, <s>Āmra</s>, <s>Kadamba</s>, <s>Nīpa</s> —

children.text: ye 'nye parārthabhavakā yamunopakūlāḥ śaṃsantu kṛṣṇapadavīṃ rahitātmanāṃ naḥ //
children.translated_text: and you other trees that exist for the sake of others, dwelling on the banks of the <s>Yamunā</s> — tell us, whose selves are lost, the path of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>!'

body.text: phalādibhiḥ sarvaprāṇināṃ saṃtarpakā ete paśyeyur iti pṛcchanti-cūteti | cūtāmrayor avāntarajātibhedaḥ kadambanīpayoś ca | he cūtādayaḥ, ye 'nye ca parārthabhavakāḥ parārtham eva bhavo janma yeṣāṃ te | yamunopakūlās tasyāḥ kūlasamīpe vartamānāḥ | tīrthavāsina ity arthaḥ | te bhavanto rahitātmanāṃ śūnyacetasāṃ naḥ kṛṣṇapadavīṃ kṛṣṇasya mārgaṃ śaṃsantu kathayantu ||BhPC_10,30.9||
body.translated_text: Thinking that these, who nourish all living beings with fruits and the like, might have seen [Him], they ask. Between <s>cūta</s> and <s>āmra</s> there is a subordinate species difference, as also between <s>kadamba</s> and <s>nīpa</s>. O <s>cūta</s> and others, and you other trees whose birth is for the sake of others, dwelling near the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.

children.text: kiṃ te kṛtaṃ kṣiti tapo bata keśavāṅghrisparśotsavotpulakitāṅgaruhair vibhāsi /
children.translated_text: 'O Earth, what austerity have you performed? You shine with your body-hairs standing erect in the ecstasy of the touch of <s>Keśava</s>'s feet!

children.text: apy aṅghrisambhava urukramavikramād vā āho varāhavapuṣaḥ parirambhaṇena //
children.translated_text: Is it from the footfall of the wide-striding <s>Urukrama</s>, or from the embrace of the boar-formed one (<s>Varāha</s>)?'

body.text: he kṣiti kṣite, tvayā kiṃ tapaḥ kṛtaṃ yā tvaṃ keśavāṅghrisparśotsavā keśavasyāṅghrisparśenotsavo yasyāḥ sā | kutaḥ | aṅgaruhair utpulakitā romāñcitā vibhāsi śobhase | tatra viśeṣaṃ pṛcchati-api kim ayam utsavo 'ṅghrisaṃbhavo 'dhunā tavaikadeśāṅghrisparśasaṃbhūtaḥ | yadvā naitāvat kintu urukramavikramāt pūrvam eva trivikramasya padā sarvākramaṇāt | aho athavā | naitāvad eva, api tu tato 'pi pūrvaṃ varāhasya vapuṣaḥ parirambhaṇeneti | atas tvayā nūnaṃ dṛṣṭas taṃ darśayeti ||BhPC_10,30.10||
body.translated_text: O Earth — what austerity was performed by you, who have an ecstatic festival at the touch of <s>Keśava</s>'s feet? How so? You shine with your body-hairs standing erect (blades of grass bristling). Regarding the specific [question]: Is this ecstasy born of the footfall — from the touch of one part of His foot now — or from the stride of <s>Urukrama</s> (<s>Vāmana</s>)?

children.text: apy eṇapatny[*27] upagataḥ priyayeha gātrais tanvan dṛśāṃ sakhi sunirvṛtim acyuto vaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'O doe, has <s>Acyuta</s> come here with His beloved, delighting your eyes with His limbs, O friend?

children.text: kāntāṅgasaṅgakucakuṅkumarañjitāyāḥ kundasrajaḥ kulapater iha vāti gandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: The fragrance of the <s>kunda</s> (jasmine) garland of the chief of the clan wafts here, tinted with saffron from the breasts [pressed] against the beloved's body.'

body.text: [*27] eṇapatnīti "patyur no yajñasaṃyoge" iti sūtrād eṇānāṃ bhavāntarayajñair yājñikatvaṃ | eṇyā yajñapatnītvam iti dṛṣṭa-praśaṃsā |
body.translated_text: '<s>Eṇapatnī</s>' — according to the <s>sūtra</s> 'of the husband at the conjunction of sacrifice,' the deer have the status of sacrificers through their inter-life sacrifices; the doe's status as 'wife of the sacrificer' — this is a praise of [their] perception.

body.text: hariṇyā dṛṣṭipratyāsattyā kṛṣṇadarśanaṃ saṃbhāvyāhuḥ-apīti | he sakhi eṇapatni, api kim upagataḥ samīpaṃ gataḥ | gātraiḥ sundarair mukhabāhvādibhiḥ | priyayā saheti yad uktaṃ tatra dyotakam | kāṇtāyā aṅgasaṅgas tena tatkucakuṅkumena rañjitāyāḥ kundakusumasrajo gandhaḥ | kulapateḥ śrīkṛṣṇasya | vātyāgacchati ||BhPC_10,30.11||
body.translated_text: Considering the possibility of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s sight through proximity to the doe's vision, they say: 'O friend, doe, has He come near? With His beautiful limbs — face, arms, and so forth. "With the beloved" — this is indicated by what was said. The <s>kunda</s> garland of the beloved one, tinted by the saffron of her breasts pressed against the body of the beloved.'

children.text: bāhuṃ priyāṃsa[*28] upadhāya gṛhītapadmo rāmānujas tulasikālikulair madāndhaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The younger brother of <s>Rāma</s>, placing His arm on the shoulder of His beloved, holding a lotus, followed here

children.text: anvīyamāna iha vas taravaḥ praṇāmaṃ kiṃ vābhinandati caran praṇayāvalokaiḥ //
children.translated_text: by bees intoxicated by the fragrance of <s>tulasī</s> — O trees, does He accept your bowing, as He walks by with loving glances?'

body.text: [*28] priyāyāḥ snigdhāyā aṃse skandhe |
body.translated_text: 'The shoulder (<s>aṃsa</s>) of the beloved, that is, of the dear one.'

body.text: phalabhāreṇa natāṃs tarūn kṛṣṇaṃ dṛṣṭvā praṇatā iti matvā priyayā saha tasya gativilāsaṃ saṃbhāvayantyaḥ pṛcchanti-bāhum iti | tulasikāyā alikulair atas tadāmodamadāndhair anvīyamāno 'nugamyamāna iha carann iti ||BhPC_10,30.12||
body.translated_text: Seeing trees bent with the weight of fruits as bowing before <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, imagining the graceful gait [of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] with His beloved, they ask: 'Placing His arm...' — followed by bees of the <s>tulasī</s> [garland], intoxicated by its fragrance, walking here.

body.text:
BhP_10,30.13
pṛcchatemā latā bāhūn apy āśliṣṭā vanaspateḥ / nūnaṃ tatkarajaspṛṣṭā bibhraty utpulakāny aho //
body.translated_text:
<s>BhP</s> 10.30.13
'Ask these creepers, [which are] embracing the arms of the lord of the forest — surely, touched by His fingernails, they bear goosebumps — oh!'

body.text: kāścid āhuḥ-he sakhyaḥ, imā latāḥ kṛṣṇena saṅgatā nūnam, ata imāḥ pṛcchata | nanu svapati-saṅgatau tatsaṅgatir durghaṭā, na | vanaspateḥ patyur bāhunāśliṣṭā api aho bhāgyaṃ nūnaṃ tan nakhaiḥ spṛṣṭā yata utpulakāni bibhrati | na hi svapatisaṅgatāv īdṛkpulakasaṃbhava iti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.13||
body.translated_text: Some say: O friends, these creepers have surely been in contact with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; therefore ask them! [One might object:] while in the embrace of their own lord [the tree], contact with Him is impossible. No — [the creepers,] though embracing the arms of the lord of the forest (their husband), are surely touched by His nails, since they bear goosebumps. For in the embrace of one's own husband, such [goosebumps] do not [normally arise].

body.text:
BhP_10,30.14
ity unmattavaco gopyaḥ kṛṣṇānveṣaṇakātarāḥ / līlā bhagavatas tās tā hy anucakrus tadātmikāḥ //
body.translated_text:
<s>BhP</s> 10.30.14
Thus the <s>gopīs</s>, speaking like madwomen, distressed in their search for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, enacted each of the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s sports, being one with Him.

body.text: unmattavat prapacchur ity etat prapañcitam idānīṃ-"ramāpates tās tā viceṣṭā jagṛhus tadātmikāḥ" iti yad uktaṃ tat prapañcayati-itīti | unmattavaco gopyaḥ unmattavacasaś ca tā gopyaś ca | kṛṣṇasyānveṣaṇena kātarā ativiḥvalāḥ | anucakrur anukṛtavatyaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.14||
body.translated_text: That they asked [the trees] like madwomen — this has been elaborated. Now the statement 'they assumed the gestures of the Lord of <s>Ramā</s>, being one with Him' is elaborated: 'Thus' — the <s>gopīs</s> who spoke like madwomen, distressed — that is, extremely distraught — by the search for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; they enacted, that is, they imitated.

body.text:
BhP_10,30.15
kasyāścit pūtanāyantyāḥ kṛṣṇāyanty apibat stanam / tokayitvā rudaty anyā padāhan śakaṭāyatīm //
body.translated_text:
<s>BhP</s> 10.30.15
One [<s>gopī</s>], acting as <s>Pūtanā</s>, had her breast drunk by another acting as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; pretending to be a baby, another kicked with her foot one who acted as the cart (<s>Śakaṭa</s>), crying out.

body.text: kasyāścid ity ādibhiś caturbhir anukaraṇaṃ prapañcyate, tataś caturbhis tanmayatvaṃ punar ekenānukaraṇam iti vivekaḥ | pūtanāyantyāḥ pūtanāvad ācarantyāḥ kṛṣṇavad ācarantī stanam apibat | tokāyitvā tokavad ātmānaṃ kṛtvā ||BhPC_10,30.15||
body.translated_text: With [verses beginning] 'one [gopī]' and four more, the imitation is elaborated; then with four more, their absorption [in Kṛṣṇa's identity]; then with one more, imitation again — this is the distinction. [The <s>gopī</s>] acting as <s>Pūtanā</s> — behaving like <s>Pūtanā</s> — another, acting as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, drank her breast. Having made herself like a baby (<s>toka</s>).

children.translated_text: One, acting as a demon, carried away another who was playing the part of the child <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>;
another crawled about, dragging her feet, [making sounds like] the rumbling of the cow-settlement.

body.text: [*29] ghoṣāḥ kiṅkiṇyas tāsāṃ niḥsvanaiḥ sahitāvaṅghrī karṣantī satī riṅgayāmāsa | ṇijartho 'vivakṣitaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*29] The anklet-bells (<s>ghoṣāḥ kiṅkiṇyaḥ</s>) — she walked dragging her feet along with their sounds. The causative sense is not intended.

body.text: daityāyitvā daityavat tṛṇāvartavad ātmānaṃ kṛtvā ekā kṛṣṇārbhabhāvanāṃ kṛṣṇasyārbhaṃ bālyaṃ bhāvayati yā tām anyāṃ jahāra ||BhPC_10,30.16|| ||BhPC_10,30.17||
body.translated_text: Having become like a demoness — having made herself like the demon <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>, one [<s>gopī</s>] was meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s childhood (<s>Kṛṣṇārbhabhāvanā</s>); another [<s>gopī</s> playing] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> carried her away. // BhPC_10,30.16 // // BhPC_10,30.17 //

children.text: āhūya dūragā yadvat kṛṣṇas tam anuvartatīm /
children.translated_text: Having called [her] from afar, one [<s>gopī</s>] who follows <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: veṇuṃ kvaṇantīṃ krīḍantīm anyāḥ śaṃsanti sādhv iti //
children.translated_text: playing a flute and sporting — the others say 'Well done!' //

body.text: dūragāḥ dūre vartamānā gāḥ | yadvad yathā kṛṣṇas tathāhūya taṃ kṛṣṇam anuvartamānām | anukurvatīm iti vā pāṭhaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.18|| ||BhPC_10,30.19||
body.translated_text: 'From afar' (<s>dūragāḥ</s>) means cows situated at a distance. 'Just as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [does]' — having called them thus, [she was] following that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Or the reading is 'imitating.' // BhPC_10,30.18 // // BhPC_10,30.19 //

children.text: mā bhaiṣṭa vātavarṣābhyāṃ tattrāṇaṃ vihitaṃ maya /
children.translated_text: 'Fear not from wind and rain! Protection has been provided by me!'
Having said thus, she who is making an effort, with one hand, raised the upper garment aloft. //

body.text: yatantī prayatnaṃ kurvatī ambaram uttarīyaṃ vastram unnidadhe ūrdhvaṃ dhṛtavatī ||BhPC_10,30.20|| ||BhPC_10,30.21||
body.translated_text: 'Making an effort' (<s>yatantī</s>) means exerting herself; 'the upper garment' (<s>ambaram</s>) — the cloth; 'raised aloft' (<s>unnidadhe</s>) means held upward. // BhPC_10,30.20 // // BhPC_10,30.21 //

children.translated_text: There, one [<s>gopī</s>] said: 'O cowherds! Behold the terrible forest fire!

children.text: cakṣūṃṣy āśv apidadhvaṃ vo vidhāsye kṣemam añjasā //
children.translated_text: Shut your eyes quickly! I shall create safety at once!'

body.text: apidadhvaṃ nimīlayata ||BhPC_10,30.22||
body.translated_text: 'Shut' (<s>apidadhvaṃ</s>) means 'close [your eyes].' // BhPC_10,30.22 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.23
baddhānyayā srajā kācit tanvī tatra ulūkhale / bhītā sudṛk pidhāyāsyaṃ bheje bhītiviḍambanam //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.23
One slender [<s>gopī</s>], bound there at the mortar with a garland made by another, good-eyed, covering her face, with fear adopted the imitation of fright. //

body.text: sudṛk sunayanam āsyaṃ pidhāya | sudṛk varākṣīti vā | bhīti viḍambanaṃ bhayānukaraṇam ||BhPC_10,30.23||
body.translated_text: 'Good-eyed' (<s>sudṛk</s>) means having beautiful eyes; covering the face. Or '<s>sudṛk</s>' means 'beautiful-eyed one.' 'Imitation of fright' (<s>bhītiviḍambana</s>) means mimicking fear. // BhPC_10,30.23 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.24
evaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ pṛcchamānā vṛndāvanalatās tarūn / vyacakṣata vanoddeśe padāni paramātmanaḥ //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.24
Thus, asking the creepers and trees of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> about <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, they saw in a forest clearing the footprints of the Supreme Self. //

body.text: evaṃ punar api vṛndāvane latās tarūṃś ca kṛṣṇaṃ pṛcchantyo vanoddeśe vanapradeśe | vyacakṣatāpaśyan ||BhPC_10,30.24|| ||BhPC_10,30.25||
body.translated_text: Thus, again asking the creepers and trees in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> about <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in a forest clearing — a forest area — they saw [the footprints]. // BhPC_10,30.24 // // BhPC_10,30.25 //

children.text: tais taiḥ padais tatpadavīm anvicchantyo 'grato' balāḥ /
children.translated_text: Following that trail through those various footprints, the young women ahead
saw [them] closely mingled with the footprints of a [particular] woman, and being distressed, they spoke. //

body.text: supṛktāni saṃmiśrāṇi ||BhPC_10,30.26||
body.translated_text: 'Closely mingled' (<s>supṛktāni</s>) means 'mixed together.' // BhPC_10,30.26 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.27
kasyāḥ padāni caitāni yātāyā nandasūnunā / aṃsanyastaprakoṣṭhāyāḥ kareṇoḥ kariṇā yathā //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.27
'Whose footprints are these, of one who has gone with the son of <s>Nanda</s>, with forearm placed upon his shoulder — like a she-elephant with a bull elephant?' //

body.text: tenāṃse nyastaḥ prakoṣṭho yasyāḥ | kareṇor hastinyāḥ ||BhPC_10,30.27||
body.translated_text: She whose forearm (<s>prakoṣṭha</s>) was placed upon his shoulder. '<s>Kareṇu</s>' means a she-elephant. // BhPC_10,30.27 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.28
anayārādhito nūnaṃ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ / yan no vihāya govindaḥ prīto yām anayad rahaḥ //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.28
'Surely the <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Hari</s>, the Lord, has been worshipped by this one — since, leaving us, <s>Govinda</s>, being pleased, took her away in secret.' //

body.text: raha ekāntasthānam ||BhPC_10,30.28||
body.translated_text: 'In secret' (<s>rahaḥ</s>) means a secluded place. // BhPC_10,30.28 //

children.translated_text: 'Blessed indeed, O friends, are the dust-particles from <s>Govinda</s>'s lotus-feet,

children.text: yān brahmeśo ramā devī dadhur mūrdhny aghanuttaye[*30] //
children.translated_text: which <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśa</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), and the goddess bear upon their heads, for the destruction of sin!' [*30]

body.text: [*30] agham aparādho virahaduḥkhaṃ vā |
body.translated_text: [*30] '<s>Agha</s>' means offence, or the suffering of separation.

body.text: he ālyaḥ sakhyaḥ, aho dhanyā atipuṇyā govindāṅghryabjareṇavaḥ | tatra hetuḥ-yān iti | asmābhir apy etad reṇvabhiṣekeṇa tathaiva kṛṣṇaḥ prāptuṃ śakya iti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.29||
body.translated_text: 'O friends (<s>ālyaḥ</s>)' means companions. 'Blessed' means extremely meritorious — the dust of <s>Govinda</s>'s lotus-feet. The reason is given in '<s>yān</s>' (which). The meaning is: by us too, through bathing in that very dust, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> can be attained...

children.text: tasyā amūni naḥ kṣobhaṃ kurvanty uccaiḥ[*31] padāni yat /
children.translated_text: 'Her footprints greatly disturb [*31] us,
because she alone, having taken away the <s>gopīs</s>' [all], enjoys <s>Acyuta</s>'s lips in secret [*32].' //

body.text:
[*31] uccaiḥ adhikaṃ kṣobhaṃ duḥkham |
[*32] "dhanaṃ bhuṅkte" iti pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text:
[*31] '<s>Uccaiḥ</s>' means 'exceedingly' — the disturbance, i.e., grief.
[*32] The reading '<s>dhanaṃ bhuṅkte</s>' (enjoys the wealth) also exists.

body.text: anyā āhuḥ-tasyā iti | gopīnāṃ sarvasvam | ayaṃ bhāvaḥ-bhaved[*33] evaṃ yadi tasyāḥ padāni saṃpṛktāni na bhaveyus tāni tu no duḥkhaṃ kurvantīti ||BhPC_10,30.30||
body.translated_text: Others say — 'Of her' and so on. [She enjoys] the <s>gopīs</s>' everything. The meaning is: if [*33] her footprints were not mixed [with his], they [alone] would cause us grief. // BhPC_10,30.30 //

body.text: [*33] yadi tasyāḥ padāni saṃpṛktāni na bhaveyus tarhi evaṃ kṛṣṇaprāptisādhanaṃ tatpadarajaḥsevanaṃ bhavet | tāni nu saṃpṛktāni tatpadāni no duḥkhaṃ kurvanti | tasyāḥ pādarajasā miśritatvāt kṛṣṇapādarajasa iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*33] If her footprints were not mixed [with his], then serving the dust of his feet alone would be the means of attaining <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. But those mixed footprints cause us grief...

children.text: na lakṣyante padāny atra tasyā nūnaṃ tṛṇāṅkuraiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Her footprints are not seen here — surely because of the grass-shoots,
as her delicate soles were being pricked — the beloved raised his beloved upon [his shoulders].' //

body.text: tad asaṃpṛktān kevalaṃ kṛṣṇapādareṇūn eva vicinvatyas tān dṛṣṭvā punar atyantaṃ samatapan | tad āha ślokatrayeṇa-na lakṣyanta iti | khidyatī sujāte sukumāre aṅghritale yasyās tām unninye skandham āropitavān ||BhPC_10,30.31||
body.translated_text: Those who were seeking only the unmixed footprints of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s foot-dust, having seen those [mixed prints], were again extremely tormented. This is stated in three verses beginning with 'Not seen' (<s>na lakṣyante</s>). 'Being pricked' (<s>khidyat</s>) — her well-born (<s>sujāta</s>), beautiful...

body.text:
BhP_10,30.32
atra prasūnāvacayaḥ priyārthe preyasā kṛtaḥ / prapadākramaṇa ete paśyatāsakale pade //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.32
'Here, a picking of flowers has been made by the beloved for his darling. See these incomplete footprints [showing] the impression of the front of the feet!' //

body.text: prapadābhyām ākramaṇaṃ kṣoṇīmardanaṃ yayoḥ | ata evāsakale pade paśyateti ||BhPC_10,30.32||
body.translated_text: 'The impression of the front of the feet' (<s>prapadākramaṇa</s>) means the treading [only] of the toes upon the ground. And therefore the footprints are incomplete — see [this]! // BhPC_10,30.32 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.33
keśaprasādhanaṃ tv atra kāminyāḥ kāminā kṛtam / tāni cūḍayatā kāntām upaviṣṭam iha dhruvam //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.33
'Here, the arrangement of hair was done by the lover for his beloved. He surely sat here while adorning his darling [with flowers as a crown].' //

body.text: tasyāḥ kṛṣṇajānvantarupaviṣṭāyāś cihnaṃ dṛṣṭvāhuḥ-keśaprasādhanam iti | kāntām adhikṛtya tāni prasūnāni cūḍayatā cūḍānukāreṇa badhnatā dhruvam upaviṣṭam ||BhPC_10,30.33||
body.translated_text: Having seen the mark of her sitting between <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s knees, they said — 'The hair arrangement' and so on. While making [those flowers] into a hair-crown for his darling — tying them in the manner of a <s>cūḍā</s> (topknot) — he surely sat here...

children.translated_text: 'He sported with her — he who delights in the Self [*34], the Self-sporting one, even though unbroken [by desires],

children.text: kāmināṃ darśayan dainyaṃ strīṇāṃ caiva durātmatām //
children.translated_text: showing the wretchedness of lovers and the wickedness of women.' //

body.text: [*34] "svātmarataḥ" iti pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*34] The reading '<s>svātmarataḥ</s>' also exists.

body.text: reme ity ādiśukoktiḥ | ātmarataḥ svatas tuṣṭaḥ | ātmārāmaḥ svakrīḍaḥ | akhaṇḍitaḥ strīvibhramair anākṛṣṭo 'pi tathā cet kim iti reme 'ta āha-kāminām iti ||BhPC_10,30.34|| ||BhPC_10,30.35||
body.translated_text: 'He sported' — this is the statement of <s>Śuka</s>. 'Delighting in the Self' (<s>ātmarataḥ</s>) means satisfied in himself. 'Self-sporting' (<s>ātmārāmaḥ</s>) means one whose play is within himself. 'Unbroken' (<s>akhaṇḍitaḥ</s>) means not attracted by the charms of women. If so, then why did he sport? To this he says — 'of lovers'...

body.text:
BhP_10,30.36
sā ca mene tadātmānaṃ variṣṭhaṃ sarvayoṣitām / hitvā gopīḥ kāmayānā mām asau bhajate priyaḥ //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.36
'And she considered herself the foremost of all women: "Leaving the <s>gopīs</s> who desire [him], my beloved worships me."' //

body.text: strīṇāṃ durātmatām āha-sā ceti dvābhyām | kāmo yānam āgamanasādhanaṃ yāsāṃ tā gopīr hitvā māṃ bhajata iti hetor ātmānaṃ variṣṭhaṃ mene iti ||BhPC_10,30.36|| ||BhPC_10,30.37||
body.translated_text: He states the wickedness of women — 'And she' in two [verses]. '<s>Kāma</s>' whose vehicle (<s>yāna</s>) — means of approach — [she is]; leaving those <s>gopīs</s>, 'he worships me' — for this reason, she considered herself the foremost. // BhPC_10,30.36 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.38
evam uktaḥ priyām āha skandha āruhyatām iti / tataś cāntardadhe kṛṣṇaḥ sā vadhūr anvatapyata //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.38
'Having been thus addressed, he said to his beloved: "Mount upon my shoulder." Then <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> vanished, and that woman was overcome with remorse.' //

body.text: kāmināṃ dainyaṃ darśayati-evam ukta iti | akhaṇḍitatvam āha-tataś ceti | tasyāṃ skandhārohodyatāyām antarhita ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.38||
body.translated_text: He shows the wretchedness of lovers — 'Having been thus addressed.' He shows [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s] 'unbroken' nature — 'Then.' When she was about to mount his shoulder, he disappeared — this is the meaning. // BhPC_10,30.38 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.39
hā nātha ramaṇa preṣṭha kvāsi kvāsi mahābhuja / dāsyās te kṛpaṇāyā me sakhe darśaya sannidhim //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.39
'Alas! O master, O beloved, O dearest! Where are you, where are you, O mighty-armed one? O friend, show your presence to your wretched maidservant!' //

body.text: anutāpam āha-hā nātheti ||BhPC_10,30.39||
body.translated_text: She expresses remorse — 'Alas! O master.' // BhPC_10,30.39 //

children.translated_text: Searching for the path of the <s>Bhagavān</s>, the <s>gopīs</s>, not far away,
saw their companion, bewildered and distressed by separation from the beloved. //

body.text: anvicchantyo mṛgayamāṇāḥ | avidūrataḥ samīpe ||BhPC_10,30.40|| ||BhPC_10,30.41||
body.translated_text: 'Searching' (<s>anvicchantīḥ</s>) means seeking. 'Not far away' (<s>avidūrataḥ</s>) means nearby. // BhPC_10,30.40 // // BhPC_10,30.41 //

children.text: tato 'viśan vanaṃ candra jyotsnā yāvad vibhāvyate /
children.translated_text: Then they entered the forest as far as the moonlight could be perceived;

children.text: tamaḥ praviṣṭam ālakṣya tato nivavṛtuḥ striyaḥ //
children.translated_text: seeing that darkness had entered, the women then turned back. //

body.text: tatas tayāpi sahitāḥ kṛṣṇānveṣaṇāya vanam aviśan | tato harer anveṣaṇān nivṛttāḥ ||BhPC_10,30.42||
body.translated_text: Then, together with her too, they entered the forest to search for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Then they turned back from seeking <s>Hari</s>. // BhPC_10,30.42 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.43
tanmanaskās tadalāpās tadviceṣṭās tadātmikāḥ / tadguṇān eva gāyantyo nātmagārāṇi sasmaruḥ //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.43
Their minds [absorbed] in him, their speech about him, their gestures his, their identity his — singing only his qualities, they did not remember their own homes. //

body.text: evaṃ tam aprāptā api svagṛhān naiva smṛtavatyaḥ | tadātmikāḥ sa evātmā yāsāṃ tāḥ | tanmayya ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,30.43||
body.translated_text: Thus, even though they did not attain him, they did not even remember their own homes. '<s>Tadātmikāḥ</s>' — those for whom he alone was the self — that is, those who had become one with him. // BhPC_10,30.43 //

body.text:
BhP_10,30.44
punaḥ pulinam āgatya kālindyāḥ kṛṣṇabhāvanāḥ / samavetā jaguḥ kṛṣṇaṃ tadāgamanakāṅkṣitāḥ //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,30.44
Returning again to the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), absorbed in meditation on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, they assembled and sang of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, longing for his coming. //

body.text: kintu pūrvaṃ yatra śrīkṛṣṇena saṅgatir āsīt tad eva kālindyāḥ puliam āgatya kṛṣṇaṃ bhāvayanti dhyāyantīti tathā tāḥ kṛṣṇasyāgamanaṃ kāṅkṣitaṃ yāsāṃ tāḥ militāḥ satyaḥ kṛṣṇam eva jagur iti ||BhPC_10,30.44||
body.translated_text: But having come to that very bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> where previously the meeting with <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> had taken place, meditating on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — thus those [<s>gopīs</s>] who longed for <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s coming...

body.text: iti śrīmadbhāgavate mahāpurāṇe daśamaskandhe pūrvārdhe bhāvārthadīpikāyāṃ ṭīkāyāṃ triṃśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ **30**
body.translated_text: Thus ends the thirtieth chapter in the <s>Bhāvārthadīpikā</s> commentary on the first half of the tenth book of the glorious <s>Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>. **30**

children.translated_text: In the thirty-first [chapter]: those who had lost hope, having returned again to the bank,
