singing along with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, pray for his coming. // 1 //
The <s>gopīs</s> said:

children.text: jayati[*35] te 'dhikaṃ janmanā vrajaḥ śrayata indirā śaśvad atra hi /
children.translated_text: 'By your birth, <s>Vraja</s> excels greatly [*35]; <s>Indirā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) forever resides here!

children.text: dayita dṛśyatāṃ[*36] dikṣu tāvakās tvayi dhṛtāsavas tvāṃ vicinvate //
children.translated_text: O beloved, may you be seen [*36] in all directions! Your [devotees], whose life-breaths are fixed on you, are searching for you!'

body.text:
[*35] jayatītyādiślokeṣu prāyaścaturṇāṃ pādānāṃ dvitīyākṣarahalaikyaṃ keṣucit pādeṣu prathamasaptamākṣarahalaikyaṃ tatra kvacit śasabavādīnām ālaṅkārikādisamayasiddhasāvarṇyād aikyam iti jñeyam |
[*36] tvayā dṛśyatāṃ pratyakṣībhūyatām iti preraṇātyāgenākarmakatvād bhāve loṭ | yadvā asmābhir bhavān dṛśyatām iti karmaṇi loṭ |
body.translated_text: [*35] In the verses beginning with '<s>jayati</s>' etc., in mostly four <s>pādas</s> (quarters), the second syllable is identical in sound; in some <s>pādas</s>, the first and seventh syllables are identical in sound — thus

body.text: jayatīti | he dayita, te janmanā vrajo 'dhikaṃ yathā bhavati tathā jayaty utkarṣeṇa vartate | yasmāt tvam atra jātas tasmad indirā lakṣmīr atra hi śrayate vrajam alaṅkṛtya vartate | evaṃ vraje sarvasmin modamāne 'tra tu tāvakās tvadīyā gopījanās tvayi tvadartham eva kathañcid dhṛtā asavo yais te tvāṃ vicinvate | atas tvayā dṛṣyatāṃ pratyakṣībhūyatām iti | yadvā asmābhir bhavān dṛṣyatām | yadvā evaṃ tvayā dṛṣyatām ete vicinvata iti ||BhPC_31.1||
body.translated_text: '<s>Jayati</s>' etc. | O beloved, by your birth, <s>Vraja</s> conquers (<s>jayati</s>), i.e., excels with distinction — because you were born here, therefore...

children.translated_text: With a glance that steals the beauty of the core of a perfect lotus born in the clear lake of autumn,

children.text: suratanātha te 'śulkadāsikā varada nighnato neha kiṃ vadhaḥ //
children.translated_text: O lord of love, we are your unpurchased maidservants — O boon-giver, when you slay [us], is that not murder? //

body.text: [*37] athavā dṛśaiva śulkadāsikāḥ dṛgrūpaśulkenaiva dāsīr api tyāgena mārayataḥ iti yojanā |
body.translated_text: [*37] Alternatively, by the glance alone [we are made] maidservants — the interpretation is: even maidservants [purchased] by the price of [your] glance alone, you slay by abandonment. |

body.text: atra svatantrāṇāṃ bāhūnāṃ vaktṛtvād aparā āhur iti sarvaślokeṣv avatāraṇā, athāpi saṅgatir ucyate | tatra vicinvantu mama kim iti cet tatrāhuḥ-śaradeti | śarad udāśaye śaratkālīne sarasi sādhu jātaṃ samyak jātaṃ yat sarasijaṃ vikasitaṃ padmaṃ tasyodare garbhe yā śrīs tāṃ muṣṇāti haratīti tathā tayā dṛśā netreṇa he suratanātha saṃbhogapate varadābhīṣṭaprada, aśulkadāsikā amūlyadāsīr no nighnato mārayatas te tava tvayā kriyamāṇa iha loke 'yaṃ vadho na bhavati kim | śastreṇaiva vadho vadhaḥ kiṃ dṛśā vadho na bhavati, kintu bhavaty eva | atas tava dṛśā 'pahṛtaprāṇapratyarpaṇāya tvayā dṛśyatām iti bhāvaḥ | tvayā dṛśyatām iti yathāsaṃbhavaṃ sarvatra vākyaśeṣaḥ ||BhPC_31.2||
body.translated_text: Here, because the many independent [<s>gopīs</s>] are speakers, [the phrase] 'others say' is the introduction to all verses; moreover, the connection is stated. There, 'may they search for me'...

children.translated_text: From the poisonous water, from the serpent-demon, from the storm wind, from the lightning fire,

children.text: vṛṣamayātmajād[*38] viśvato bhayād ṛṣabha te vayaṃ rakṣitā muhuḥ //
children.translated_text: from the bull-demon and the <s>Māya</s>-born demon, from every danger — O best of men, you have protected us again and again! //

body.text: [*38] vṛṣātmajo vatsāsuraḥ "varāhatokoniragād" itivat | mayātmajo vyomāsuraḥ | taccaritram agre vakṣyamāṇam api rāsāt pūrvabhāvīti jñeyam |
body.translated_text: [*38] '<s>Vṛṣātmaja</s>' is the bull-demon (<s>Vatsāsura</s>), as in [the expression] 'the boar-calf emerged.' '<s>Mayātmaja</s>' is the demon <s>Vyoma</s>. His story, though to be narrated later, is referred to as if past, since it was prior to the <s>Rāsa</s> [dance]...

body.text: kiṃ ca bahubhyo mṛtyubhyaḥ kṛpayā rakṣitvā kimitīdānīṃ dṛśā manmathaṃ preṣya ghātayasīty āhuḥ-viṣeti | he ṛṣabha śreṣṭha, viṣamayāj jalādyo 'pyayo nāśas tasmāt tathā vyālarākṣasād aghāsurād varṣān mārutād vaidyutānalād aśanipātāt vṛṣo 'ṛṣṭas[*39] tasmān mayātmajād vyomād viśvato 'nyasmād api sarvato bhayāc ca kāliyadamanādinā rakṣitāḥ kim idānīm upekṣasa iti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_31.3||
body.translated_text: Moreover, having compassionately saved [us] from many forms of death, why now do you send <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) through [your] glance to slay [us]? — thus they say with '<s>viṣa</s>' etc. | O '<s>ṛṣabha</s>' (best one), O foremost one...

children.text: na khalu gopīkānandano bhavān akhiladehinām antarātmadṛk /
children.translated_text: You are not merely the son of a cowherd woman; you are the inner self who sees all embodied beings.

children.text: vikhanasārthito viśvaguptaye sakha udeyivān sātvatāṃ kule //
children.translated_text: Sought by <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>Vikhanasā</s>) for the protection of the universe, O friend, you have risen in the clan of the <s>Sātvatas</s>. //

body.text: [*39] ariṣṭavyomāsurayor vadhasya bhāvitve 'pi gargādimukhāc chrutatvena vipralambapoṣakatvena vā bhūtavan nirdeśaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*39] Although the slaying of <s>Ariṣṭa</s> and <s>Vyomāsura</s> is [yet to come], the reference is in the past tense either because it was heard from the mouth of <s>Garga</s> and others, or because it nourishes the deceptive concealment [of his divinity]. |

body.text: api ca viśvapālanāyāvatīrṇasya tava bhaktopekṣā 'tyantam anucitety āśayenāhuḥ-na khalv iti | he sakhe, bhavān khalu niścitaṃ yaśodāsuto na bhavati, kintu sarvaprāṇināṃ buddhisākṣī | nanu sa kiṃ dṛśyo bhavati tatrāhuḥ-vikhanasā brahmaṇā viśvapālanāya prārthitaḥ sansātvatāṃ kule udeyivān udita iti ||BhPC_31.4||
body.translated_text: Moreover, with the intent that neglect of devotees is utterly unfitting for one who has descended for the protection of the universe — they say '<s>na khalu</s>' etc. | O friend, you are certainly, without doubt...

children.text: viracitābhayaṃ vṛṣṇidhūrya te caraṇam[*40] īyuṣāṃ saṃsṛter bhayāt /
children.translated_text: Your lotus foot, which has bestowed fearlessness, O chief of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, upon those who approach [it] out of fear of <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth),

children.text: karasaroruhaṃ kānta[*41] kāmadaṃ śirasi dhehi naḥ śrīkaragraham //
children.translated_text: O beloved, that wish-fulfilling lotus-hand — place it upon our heads, [that hand] which holds the hand of <s>Śrī</s> (the Goddess of Fortune)! //

body.text:
[*40] "śaraṇam īyuṣām" iti pāṭhaḥ |
[*41] yadvā kāntaṃ ca tatkāmadaṃ ceti svataḥ sukharūpam abhīṣṭadaṃ ceti kecit |
body.translated_text: [*40] The reading '<s>śaraṇam īyuṣām</s>' [is also found]. | [*41] Alternatively, '<s>kāntam</s>' and '<s>kāmadam</s>' separately — inherently of the nature of bliss and granting desires — thus some [interpret]. |

body.text: tasmāt tvadbhaktānām asmākam etat prārthanācatuṣṭayaṃ saṃpādayety āhuḥ-viracitābhayam ity ādi caturbhiḥ | he vṛṣṇidhurya, saṃsṛter bhayāt te caraṇam īyuṣāṃ śaraṇaṃ prāptānāṃ prāṇināṃ viracitaṃ dattam abhayaṃ yena tat tathā he kānta, kāmadaṃ varadaṃ tathā śriyaḥ karaṃ gṛhṇātīti tathā tad bhavatkarasaroruhaṃ na śirasi dehi ||BhPC_31.5||
body.translated_text: Therefore, fulfill these four requests of ours, your devotees — they say with '<s>viracitābhayam</s>' etc., in four [verses]. | O chief of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>, [your] foot, [which is approached] by those in fear of <s>saṃsāra</s>...

children.translated_text: O destroyer of the sufferings of the people of <s>Vraja</s>! O hero! Your smile destroys the pride of your own people! O friend,

children.text: bhaja sakhe bhavatkiṅkarīḥ[*42] sma no jalaruhānanaṃ cāru darśaya //
children.translated_text: accept us, your maidservants! Show us your beautiful lotus face! //

body.text: [*42] athavā abhavatkiṅkarīḥ anyā eva bhaja | mukhapadmaṃ ca no pradarśaya | maraṇasyaiva niścitatvād iti praṇayakope yojanā |
body.translated_text: [*42] Alternatively, '<s>abhavatkiṅkarīḥ</s>' — accept [us who are] not [yet] your maidservants, i.e., others. And show us your lotus face. Since death is already certain — this is the interpretation in the mood of amorous anger. |

body.text: he vrajajanārtihan he vīra, nija janānāṃ yaḥ smayo garvas tasya dhvaṃsanaṃ nāśakaṃ smitaṃ yasya tathābhūta he sakhe, bhavatkiṅkarīr no 'smān bhaja āśraya | smeti niścitam | prathamaṃ tāvaj jalaruhānanaṃ cāru yoṣitāṃ no darśaya ||BhPC_31.6||
body.translated_text: O destroyer of the sufferings of the people of <s>Vraja</s>, O hero — whose smile destroys (<s>dhvaṃsana</s>) the pride (<s>smaya</s>) of his own people (<s>nija-janānām</s>) — O friend, accept (<s>bhaja</s>) us, your maidservants (<s>bhavatkiṅkarīḥ</s>)...

children.translated_text: [Your] lotus foot, which removes the sins of those who bow down, which follows the grass-grazers [cows], which is the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune),

children.text: phaṇiphaṇārpitaṃ[*43] te padāmbujaṃ kṛṇu kuceṣu naḥ kṛndhi hṛcchayam //
children.translated_text: which was placed upon the hoods of the serpent [<s>Kāliya</s>] — place it upon our breasts! Destroy the fever of our hearts! //

body.text: [*43] phaṇinaḥ phaṇāsv arpaṇamātreṇa tadviṣadarpasyeva hṛdi sparśamātreṇa kandarpasya nāśo na duṣkara iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*43] By the mere placement upon the serpent's hoods, just as the pride of his poison [was destroyed], so the mere touch upon the heart [destroys] <s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid) — this is not difficult — such is the purport. |

body.text: aviśeṣeṇa praṇatāṇāṃ dehināṃ pāpakarśanaṃ pāpahantṛ tṛṇacarān paśūn apy anu gacchati kṛpayeti tathā saubhāgyena śriyo niketanaṃ vīryātirekeṇa phaṇinaḥ phanāsv arpitaṃ te padāmbujaṃ naḥ kuceṣu kṛṇu kuru | kim artham | hṛcchayaṃ kāmaṃ kṛndhi chindhi ||BhPC_31.7||
body.translated_text: [Your] foot, which without distinction removes the sins of those embodied beings who bow down, which follows even the grass-grazers, i.e., the cattle, out of compassion, which by its beauty is the abode of <s>Śrī</s>, and by its excess of power, [was placed] upon the serpent's [hood]...

children.translated_text: With your sweet voice, with charming words that delight the wise, O lotus-eyed one,

children.text: vidhikarīr[*44] imā vīra muhyatīr adharasīdhunāpyāyayasva naḥ //
children.translated_text: O hero, revive us, your obedient ones, who are swooning — with the nectar of your lips! //

body.text: [*44] yadvā giraiva vidhikarīr adhunā virahāt saṃmuhyatīḥ imāḥ pratyakṣāḥ |
body.translated_text: [*44] Alternatively, with [your] voice alone [make us] your obedient ones (<s>vidhikarīḥ</s>); revive these ones who are now (<s>adhunā</s>) fainting from separation, who are [right here] before [your eyes]. |

body.text: he puṣkarekṣaṇa, tavaiva madhurayā girā valgūni vākyāni yasyāṃ tayā budhānāṃ manojñayā hṛdyayā gambhīrayety arthaḥ | muhyatīr imā no vidhikarīḥ kiṅkarīr adharasīdhunā āpyāyayasva saṃjīvayeti ||BhPC_31.8||
body.translated_text: O lotus-eyed one, with your sweet voice, in which the words are charming (<s>valgu</s>), delightful (<s>manojñayā</s>) to the wise (<s>budhānām</s>), i.e., profound in meaning — revive us who are swooning, your maidservants (<s>vidhikarīḥ</s>, i.e., <s>kiṅkarīḥ</s>)...

children.text: tava kathāmṛtaṃ[*45] taptajīvanaṃ kavibhir īḍitaṃ kalmaṣāpaham /
children.translated_text: The nectar of your stories — the life of the afflicted, praised by sages, destroying sins,

children.text: śravaṇamaṅgalaṃ śrīmad ātataṃ bhuvi gṛṇanti te bhūridā janāḥ //
children.translated_text: auspicious to hear, glorious, spread throughout the world — those who recite them are the most generous of people! //

body.text: [*45] yadvā santaptā āhuḥ-tava kathā eva ṃrtaṃ mṛtiḥ saivoddīpanavidhayāsmān mārayati | tathā taptajīvanaṃ tapte taile jīvanam ivety arthaḥ | tathā ca ye 'smat purato gṛṇanti te bhūridā mahāghātakāḥ | "do avakhaṇḍane" iti dhātuḥ | ataḥ kathāmṛtenālam iti yojanā |
body.translated_text: [*45] Alternatively, the afflicted ones say: your story is itself '<s>amṛtam</s>' (death/nectar) — it is death itself, and by the method of intensification it kills us. Also, '<s>taptajīvanam</s>' — like living in hot oil — this is the meaning. And thus...

body.text: kiṃ ca asmākaṃ tvadvirahe prāptam eva mataṇaṃ kintu tvatkathāmṛtaṃ pāyayadbhiḥ sukṛtibhir vañcitam ity āhuḥ-taveti | kathaivāmṛtam | atra hetuḥ-taptajīvanam | prasiddhāmṛtād utkarṣam āhuḥ-kavibhir brahmavidbhir apīḍitaṃ stutam | devabhogyaṃ tv amṛtaṃ tair tucchīkṛtam | kiṃ ca kalmaṣāpahaṃ kāmakarmanirasanam | tattvamṛtaṃ naivaṃbhūtam | kiṃ ca śravaṇamaṅgalaṃ śravaṇamātreṇa maṅgalapradam | tat tv anuṣṭhānāpekṣam | kiṃ ca śrīmat suśāntam | tat tu mādakam | evaṃbhūtaṃ tvatkathāmṛtam ātataṃ yathā bhavati tathā ye bhuvi gṛṇanti nirūpayanti te janā bhūridā bahudātāraḥ | jīvitaṃ dadatīty arthaḥ | yadvā evaṃbhūtaṃ tvatkathāmṛtaṃ ye bhuvi gṛṇanti te bhūridāḥ pūrvajanmasu bahu dattavantaḥ sukṛtina ity arthaḥ | etad uktaṃ bhavati-ye kevalaṃ kathāmṛtaṃ gṛṇanti te 'pi tāvad atidhanyāḥ kiṃ punar ye tvāṃ paśyanti, ataḥ prārthayāmahe tvayā dṛśyatām iti ||BhPC_31.9||
body.translated_text: Moreover, death has indeed befallen us in separation from You, but we have been cheated by the virtuous ones who make us drink the nectar of Your stories — thus they say with ‘tava.’ The stories themselves are nectar. The reason for this: ‘reviving the dead.’ They declare its superiority over the well-known nectar: it is praised even by poets, by knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. The nectar enjoyed by the gods, however, is considered trivial by them. Moreover, it removes sins — it destroys desire and karma. That nectar is not of such nature. Moreover, it is auspicious merely upon hearing — it bestows auspiciousness by mere hearing alone. That [ordinary nectar] however requires [actual] practice. Moreover, it is beautiful and supremely peaceful. That [ordinary nectar] however is intoxicating. Those people on earth who proclaim, who expound such nectar of Your stories as it extends — they are ‘bhūridā,’ great givers. The meaning is: they give life itself. Alternatively, those on earth who proclaim such nectar of Your stories are ‘bhūridā’ — meaning they have given much in previous births and are thus meritorious. What is conveyed is this: those who merely recite the nectar of [Your] stories are themselves extremely fortunate; how much more so those who see You! Therefore we beseech [You]: may You be seen [by us]! ||BhPC_31.9||

children.text: prahasitaṃ priya premavīkṣaṇaṃ viharaṇaṃ ca te dhyānamaṅgalam[*46] /
children.translated_text: Your laughter, O beloved, Your loving glance, / Your pastimes that are auspicious even in meditation[*46],

children.text: rahasi saṃvido yā hṛdi spṛśaḥ kuhaka no manaḥ kṣobhayanti hi //
children.translated_text: the intimate conversations that touch the heart with the arising of desire — / O deceiver, they agitate our minds! //

body.text: [*46] dhyānamātreṇa maṅgalapradam | idaṃ prahasitādīnāṃ viśeṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: [*46] ‘Auspicious even in meditation’ means bestowing auspiciousness through meditation alone. This is the qualifier of laughter and the rest.

body.text: nanu matkathāśravaṇenaiva nirvṛtā bhavata kiṃ maddarśanena, na, tvadvilāsakṣubhitacittā vayaṃ tatrāpi śāntiṃ na vindāma ity āhuḥ-prahasitam iti | he priya, kuhaka kapaṭa, saṃvidaḥ saṅketanarmāṇi ||BhPC_31.10||
body.translated_text: Now [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> might say:] ‘Be content with merely hearing My stories; what need of My direct presence?’ ‘No, our minds are agitated by Your playful acts, and we find no peace even in that’ — thus they say with ‘prahasitam.’ O beloved, O deceiver (<s>kuhaka</s>), O fraudulent one! The ‘conversations’ are the intimate jests and agreements. ||BhPC_31.10||

children.text: calasi yad vrajāc cārayan paśūn nalinasundaraṃ nātha te padam /
children.translated_text: When You go from <s>Vraja</s> herding the cattle, O lord, Your lotus-beautiful foot,

children.text: śilatṛṇāṅkuraiḥ sīdatīti naḥ kalilatāṃ manaḥ kānta gacchati //
children.translated_text: it is pained by stones, thorns, and sprouts — at this thought / our minds, O beloved, become distressed. //

body.text: kiṃ ca tvayi vayam atipremārdracittās tvaṃ punar asmāsu kena hetunā kapaṭam ācarasīty āhuḥ ślokadvayena-calasīti | he nātha he kānta, yat yadā vrajāc calasi paśūṃś cārayaṃs tadā tan nalinasundaraṃ komalaṃ te padaṃ śilaiḥ kaṇiśais tṛṇair aṅkuraiś ca sīdati kliśyed iti no manaḥ kalilatām asvāsthyaṃ gacchati prāpnoti | evaṃbhūtās tvadduḥkhaśaṅkitacittā vayam ||BhPC_31.11||
body.translated_text: Moreover, we whose hearts are exceedingly tender with love toward You — for what reason do You practice deception toward us? — thus they say in two verses, beginning with ‘calasi.’ O lord, O beloved, when You go from <s>Vraja</s> herding the cattle, then that lotus-beautiful, tender foot of Yours is pained by stones, pebbles, thorns, and sprouts — at this [thought] our minds attain distress and unease. Such are we, with minds anxious about Your suffering. ||BhPC_31.11||

children.translated_text: At the close of day, wearing Your face like a forest-flower, / covered with dark curls,

children.text: ghanarajasvalaṃ darśayan muhur manasi naḥ smaraṃ vīra yacchasi //
children.translated_text: thick with dust, showing it again and again, / You plant in our minds only longing (<s>smara</s>), O hero. //

body.text: tvaṃ tu dinaparikṣaye sāyaṃ kāle nīlakuntalair āvṛtaṃ ghanarajasvalaṃ gorajaś churitaṃ vanaruhānanam alimālākulaparāgacchuritapadmatulyam ānanaṃ bibhrat tac ca muhur muhur darśayan no manasi kevalaṃ smaraṃ[*47] yacchasy arpayasi | na tu saṅgaṃ dadāsīti kapaṭas tvam iti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_31.12||
body.translated_text: But You, at the close of day, in the evening time, bearing a face covered with dark curls, thick with the dust of cow-herding, resembling a lotus dusted with pollen and surrounded by rows of bees — and showing that [face] again and again, You plant in our minds only <s>Smara</s> (love/remembrance)[*47]. But You do not give [us] Your company — this is the purport: You are deceitful. ||BhPC_31.12||

body.text: [*47] smaraṃ smaraṇamātreṇāpi kṣobhakam |
body.translated_text: [*47] ‘<s>Smara</s>’ is that which agitates even through mere remembrance.

children.translated_text: Your lotus foot, which grants the desires of those who bow, which is worshipped by <s>Padmaja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), / which adorns the earth[*48], which is to be meditated upon in calamity,

children.text: caraṇapaṅkajaṃ śantamaṃ ca te ramaṇa naḥ staneṣv arpayādhihan //
children.translated_text: and which is supremely blissful — O lord, place it upon our breasts, / O delighter! //

body.text: [*48] dharaṇiṃ dhvajādicihnair maṇḍayatīti |
body.translated_text: [*48] ‘Adorning the earth’ means it adorns the earth with the marks of flag, thunderbolt, and other [auspicious signs].

body.text: ato 'dhunā kapaṭaṃ vihāyaivaṃ kurv iti prārthayanti ślokadvayena-praṇatakāmadam iti | he adhihan he ramaṇa, padmajena brahmaṇārcitam āpadi dhyeyaṃ dhyānamātreṇāpannivartakaṃ śantamaṃ ca sevāsamaye 'pi sukhatamaṃ te caraṇapaṅkajaṃ kāmatāpaśāntaye naḥ staneṣv arpayeti ||BhPC_31.13||
body.translated_text: Therefore, now abandoning deceit, do thus! — they entreat in two verses, beginning with ‘praṇata.’ O lord (<s>adhihan</s>), O delighter (<s>ramaṇa</s>)! Worshipped by <s>Padmaja</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>), to be meditated upon in calamity — [meaning] averting misfortune through mere meditation — and supremely blissful even at the time of service: place that lotus foot of Yours upon our breasts, for the quenching of the fever of desire! ||BhPC_31.13||

children.translated_text: That which increases love-play, that which destroys sorrow, / that which is well-kissed by the resonating flute,

children.text: itararāgavismāraṇaṃ nṛṇāṃ[*49] vitara vīra nas te 'dharāmṛtam //
children.translated_text: that which causes people[*49] to forget all other attachments — / bestow upon us, O hero, the nectar of Your lips! //

body.text: [*49] nṛṇām iti puṃsām api, kim uta nārīṇām |
body.translated_text: [*49] ‘Of men’ — meaning even of men, how much more so of women!

body.text: api ca he vīra, te 'dharāmṛtaṃ no vitara dehi | svaritena nāditena veṇunā suṣṭhu cumbitam iti nādāmṛtavāsitam iti bhāvaḥ | itararāgavismāraṇaṃ nṛṇām itareṣu sārvabhaumādisukheṣu rāgam icchāṃ vismārayati vilāpayatīti tathā tat ||BhPC_31.14||
body.translated_text: Moreover, O hero, give us, bestow upon us, the nectar of Your lips! ‘Well-kissed by the resonating flute’ — the purport is: perfumed with the nectar of [its] sound. ‘Causing forgetfulness of other attachments in people’ — it causes to forget, it dissolves, the desire and longing for other [pleasures] such as imperial happiness. ||BhPC_31.14||

children.text: aṭati yad bhavān ahni kānanaṃ truṭir yugāyate tvām apaśyatām /
children.translated_text: When You wander in the forest during the day, / for us who cannot see You, a moment (<s>truṭi</s>) becomes an age (<s>yuga</s>).

children.text: kuṭilakuntalaṃ śrīmukhaṃ ca te jaḍa[*50] udīkṣatāṃ pakṣmakṛd dṛśām //
children.translated_text: And when seeing Your beautiful face with curling locks, / O fool[*50], the creator of eyelids for our eyes [seems blameworthy]! //

body.text: [*50] yadvā ajaḍa iti chedaḥ | yaḥ pakṣmāṇi kṛntati sa nimīlanābhāvasaṃpādaka eva ajaḍo rasajñaḥ | kiṃ vā svadṛśāṃ pakṣmacchideva ajaḍaḥ udīkṣatāṃ uccaiḥ paśyatu | vayaṃ tu pakṣmapihitadṛśo jaḍāḥ kiṃ paśyāmeti darśane 'pi vidhāna duḥkham iti bhāvaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*50] Alternatively, the word-division is ‘ajaḍa’ (‘O wise one!’). He who cuts the eyelids — that is, the one who creates the absence of closing [the eyes] — is the wise connoisseur of <s>rasa</s>. Or: may the cutting of our eyelids look upward, gazing intently! But we, with eyes covered by eyelids, are the foolish ones — what do we see? The purport is: there is suffering even in seeing.

body.text: kiṃ ca kṣaṇam api tvadadarśane duḥkhaṃ darśane ca sukhaṃ dṛṣṭvā sarvasaṅgaparityāgena yataya iva vayaṃ truṭiḥ kṣaṇārdham api yugavad bhavati | evam adarśane duḥkham uktam | punaś ca kathañcid dinānte te tava śrīman mukham uduccair īkṣamānānāṃ teṣāṃ dṛṣāṃ pakṣmakṛd brahmā jaḍo manda eva | nimeṣamātram apy antaram asahyam iti darśane sukham uktam ||BhPC_31.15||
body.translated_text: Moreover, in not seeing You even for a moment there is suffering, and in seeing [You] there is happiness. Having seen [You], like renunciants who have abandoned all attachments — such are we: even half a moment (<s>truṭi</s>) becomes like an age (<s>yuga</s>). Thus the suffering of non-seeing has been stated. Furthermore, when somehow at the end of the day, as we gaze upward at Your beautiful face, <s>Brahmā</s>, the creator of eyelids for those eyes, [seems] foolish, dull indeed. The suffering of [even momentary blinking during] seeing has [also] been stated — [meaning] even a moment’s interruption is unbearable. ||BhPC_31.15||

children.translated_text: Having transgressed husbands, sons, family, brothers, and kinsmen, / we have come to Your presence, O <s>Acyuta</s>.

children.text: gatividas tavodgītamohitāḥ kitava yoṣitaḥ kas tyajen niśi //
children.translated_text: O knower of [our] intentions, [we are] enchanted by Your song, / O cheat — what [man] would abandon women [who come to him] at night? //

body.text: tasmāt he acyuta, patīn sutān anvayāṃs tatsaṃbandhino bhrātṝn bāndhavāṃś cātivilaṅghya tava samīpam āgatā vayam | kathaṃbhūtasya | gativido 'smad āgamanaṃ jānataḥ, gītagatīr vā jānataḥ, gativido vayaṃ vā | tavodgītenoccair gītena mohitāḥ he kitava śaṭha, evaṃbhūtā yoṣito niśi svayam āgatās tvām ṛte kas tyajet | na ko 'pīty arthaḥ ||BhPC_31.16||
body.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Acyuta</s>, having transgressed husbands, sons, members of the family and their relations, brothers, and kinsmen, we have come to Your proximity. Of what nature [is He]? ‘Knower of intentions’ — knowing our arrival; or knowing the modes of song; or ‘we are the knowers of intentions.’ Enchanted by Your loud singing — O cheat (<s>kitava</s>), O rogue! What [man] would abandon women of such nature who have come of their own accord at night? No one at all — this is the meaning. ||BhPC_31.16||

children.translated_text: The intimate conversations[*51], the arising of heart’s desire, / the laughing face, the loving glance,

children.text: bṛhaduraḥ śriyo vīkṣya dhāma te muhur atispṛhā[*52] muhyate manaḥ //
children.translated_text: and Your broad chest, the abode of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) — seeing [all this], / our minds are bewildered with intense longing[*52]. //

body.text:
[*51] rahasi saṃvido yatra tam | alugārṣaḥ | prahasitam ānanaṃ yatra | premṇā vīkṣṇaṃ yatra |
[*52] atispṛhā bhavati | yadvā spṛheti saṃpadāditvād bhāve kvipi tṛtīyā | mano vīkṣya atispṛhayā muhyatīty arthaḥ | 'atispṛhaṃ' iti citsukhapāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text:
[*51] ‘The intimate conversations’ — wherein those [take place]. Irregular Vedic usage [in the sandhi]. ‘The laughing face’ — wherein [that appears]. ‘Loving glance’ — wherein [that is present].
[*52] ‘Intense longing arises.’ Alternatively, ‘spṛhā’ with the <s>kvip</s> suffix in the sense of a state from the ‘saṃpad’ class; the instrumental case [applies]. The meaning is: the mind, seeing [all this], is bewildered through intense longing. <s>Citsukha</s>’s reading is ‘atispṛhaṃ.’

body.text: atas tvayā tyaktānām asmākaṃ prāktanatvaddarśananidānahṛdrogasya tvatsaṅgatyaiva cikitsāṃ kurvityāśayenāhur dvayena-rahasīti | śriyo dhāma te bṛhad viśālam uraś ca vīkṣyātispṛhā bhavati | tathā ca muhur muhur mano muhyati ||BhPC_31.17||
body.translated_text: Therefore, since we have been abandoned by You, the cure for the heart-disease caused by the previous sight of You is only through union with You — with this intention they speak in two [verses], beginning with ‘rahasi.’ Seeing Your broad, wide chest, the abode of <s>Śrī</s>, intense longing arises. And thus, again and again, the mind is bewildered. ||BhPC_31.17||

children.text: vrajavanaukasāṃ[*53] vyaktir aṅga te vṛjinahantry alaṃ viśvamaṅgalam /
children.translated_text: O dear one, Your manifestation among the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s> and the forest[*53] / is indeed the destroyer of affliction, the auspiciousness of the universe.

children.text: tyaja manāk ca nas tvatspṛhātmanāṃ svajanahṛdrujāṃ yan niṣūdanam //
children.translated_text: Grant to us, whose souls long for You, / even a little of that which is the cure for the heart-disease of Your own people. //

body.text: [*53] vrajaukasāṃ vanaukasāṃ ca |
body.translated_text: [*53] ‘Of the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s> and of the forest-dwellers.’

body.text: tava ca vyaktir abhivyaktir vrajavanaukasāṃ sarveṣām aviśeṣeṇa vṛjinahantrī duḥkhanirasanīti viśvamaṅgalaṃ sarvamaṅgalarūpā ca | atas tvatspṛhātmanāṃ tvatspṛhārūḍhamanasāṃ no manāg īṣat kim api tyaja muñca | kārpaṇyam akurvan dehīty arthāḥ | kiṃ tat | svajanahṛdrogāṇāṃ yad atigopyaṃ niṣūdanaṃ nivartakam auṣadhaṃ tat tvam eva vetasīti gūḍhābhiprāyam ||BhPC_31.18||
body.translated_text: Your manifestation — Your visible appearance — without any distinction for all the inhabitants of <s>Vraja</s> and the forest, is the destroyer of affliction, the remover of suffering, and universal auspiciousness, the very form of all that is auspicious. Therefore, to us whose minds are filled with longing for You, grant even a little, release even something — [this] with a tone of supplication means ‘give!’ What is that? That which is the cure, the medicine, the remedy for the heart-diseases of Your own people — that is You alone, [they] understand. This is the hidden intent. ||BhPC_31.18||

children.text: yat te sujātacaraṇāmburuhaṃ staneṣu bhītāḥ śanaiḥ priya dadhīmahi karkaśeṣu /
children.translated_text: We, afraid, would gently place Your well-born lotus foot upon our harsh breasts, / O beloved.

children.text: tenāṭavīm aṭasi tad vyathate na kiṃ svit kūrpādibhir bhramati dhīr bhavadāyuṣāṃ naḥ //
children.translated_text: Yet with that [same foot] You wander in the forest — is it not pained / by pebbles and the like? Our minds, [minds] of those whose very life is You, are bewildered. //

body.text: atipremadharṣitā rudatya āhuḥ-yad iti | he priya, yat te tava sukumāraṃ padābjaṃ kaṭhineṣu kuceṣu saṃmardanaśaṅkitāḥ śanair dadhīmahi[*54] dhārayema vayam | tvaṃ tu tenāṭavīm aṭasi | "nayasi" iti pāṭhe paśūn vā kāñcid anyāṃ vā ātmānam eva vā nayasi prāpayasi | tat tataḥ tat padāmbujaṃ vā kūrpādibhiḥ sūkṣmapāṣāṇādibhiḥ kiṃ svin na vyathate kathaṃ nu nāma na vyatheteti bhavān[*55] evāyur jīvanaṃ yāsāṃ tāsāṃ no dhīr bhramati muhyatīti ||BhPC_31.19||
body.translated_text: Overwhelmed by excessive love, weeping, they said as follows — 'O beloved, we place (<s>dadhīmahi</s>) your delicate lotus foot upon our hard breasts cautiously, fearing its bruising. Yet you wander through the forest with those [feet]. In the reading '<s>nayasi</s>', [it means] you lead the cattle, or some other person, or yourself. Therefore (<s>tat</s>), those lotus feet — do they not suffer pain from pebbles and small sharp stones? How could they not be hurt? For you are the very life (<s>āyus</s>) of us [<s>gopīs</s>], and our minds are bewildered.' ||BhPC_31.19||

body.text:
[*54] dadhīmahi dhartuṃ yogyam | "arhe kṛtyatṛcaś ca" iti liṅ |
[*55] bhavadāyuṣām iti | ittham eva ca "tvayi dhṛtāsavaḥ" ity upakramo 'pi |
body.translated_text:
[*54] '<s>Dadhīmahi</s>' means 'fit to hold.' The optative is formed by the rule '<s>arhe kṛtyatṛcaś ca</s>.' |
[*55] '[You who are] the life of these [<s>gopīs</s>]' — and similarly, the opening verse '<s>tvayi dhṛtāsavaḥ</s>' ('those whose life-breaths are sustained in you') [confirms this]. |

body.text: iti śrīmadbhāgavate mahāpurāṇe daśamaskandhe pūrvārdhe bhāvārthadīpikāyāṃ ṭīkāyāṃ ekatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ **31**
body.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the tenth book, first half, in the commentary called <s>Bhāvārthadīpikā</s>, the thirty-first chapter. **31**

children.translated_text: In the thirty-second [chapter], <s>Hari</s>, his heart melting from the lamentations born of separation,
appeared there and consoled those <s>gopīs</s>, honoring them. // 1 //
Their hearts overwhelmed by the waves of the nectar of his own love,

children.text: sad ayaṃ nandayan gopīr udgato nandanandanaḥ // 2 //
children.translated_text: the son of <s>Nanda</s> arose, gladdening the <s>gopīs</s>. // 2 //

children.text: iti gopyaḥ pragāyantyaḥ pralapantyaś ca citradhā /
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>gopīs</s>, singing and lamenting in various ways,
wept aloud, O King, yearning for the sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. //

body.text: iti gopya iti | ity evaṃ prabhṛti | citradhā anekadhā susvaram uccaiḥ kṛṣṇadarśane lālasātispṛhā yāsāṃ tāḥ ||BhPC_10,32.1||
body.translated_text: 'Thus the <s>gopīs</s>' — 'thus' means 'in this manner and so forth.' '<s>Citradhā</s>' means 'in manifold ways'; '<s>susvaram</s>' means 'loudly'; those whose intense longing (<s>lālasā</s>) was for the sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||BhPC_10,32.1||

children.translated_text: Before them appeared <s>Śauri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), his lotus face smiling,
wearing yellow garments, garlanded — in person, the one who agitates even <s>Manmatha</s> (the god of love) himself. //

body.text: sākṣān manmathamanmatho jaganmohanasya kāmasyāpi manasy udbhūtaḥ kāmaḥ sākṣāt tasyāpi mohaka ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,32.2||
body.translated_text: '<s>Sākṣāt manmatha-manmathaḥ</s>' — He in whose mind love arises even toward <s>Manmatha</s>, the enchanter of the world — that is, He who in person bewilders even <s>Kāmadeva</s> himself: this is the meaning. ||BhPC_10,32.2||

children.translated_text: Seeing him, their most beloved, having arrived, the women, their eyes blossoming wide with joy,

children.text: uttasthur yugapat sarvās tanvaḥ prāṇam ivāgatam //
children.translated_text: all rose up simultaneously, like the limbs [rising to greet] the returning life-breath. //

body.text: tanvaḥ karacaraṇādayaḥ ||BhPC_10,32.3|| ||BhPC_10,32.4||
body.translated_text: '<s>Tanvaḥ</s>' means the hands, feet, and other limbs [of the body]. ||BhPC_10,32.3|| ||BhPC_10,32.4||

children.translated_text: One slender [<s>gopī</s>] received in her cupped hands the <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) he had been chewing;
another, burning [with love], placed his lotus foot upon her breasts. //

body.text: añjalinā saṃhatahastadvayena ||BhPC_10,32.5||
body.translated_text: '<s>Añjalinā</s>' means with both hands joined together. ||BhPC_10,32.5||

children.translated_text: One, knitting her brows, overwhelmed by the agitation of [her] love,
as if striking [him], gazed with sidelong glances, biting her lip. //

body.text: bhrukuṭiṃ bhruvam ābadhya kuṭilīkṛtya premasaṃrambheṇa praṇayakopāveśena vihvalā vivaśā daṣṭādharoṣṭhā kaṭāḥ kaṭākṣās tair ye ākṣepāḥ paribhavās tais tāḍayantīvaikṣat ||BhPC_10,32.6||
body.translated_text: 'Knitting the brows (<s>bhrukuṭi</s>)' means curving the eyebrows; 'overwhelmed (<s>vihvalā</s>) by the agitation of love (<s>prema-saṃrambha</s>)' means rendered helpless by the force of amorous indignation; 'with bitten lip' — with her lower lip bitten; '<s>kaṭākṣepaiḥ</s>' means sidelong glances (<s>kaṭākṣa</s>) that serve as reproaches (<s>ākṣepa</s>) — with these she gazed as if striking [him]. ||BhPC_10,32.6||

children.translated_text: Another, savoring his lotus face with unblinking eyes,

children.text: āpītam api nātṛpyat santas[*56] taccaraṇaṃ yathā //
children.translated_text: though she had drunk it in fully, was not satiated — like the saints [who are never satiated] with his feet. //

body.text: [*56] santo dāsyabhaktiniṣṭhā iti tṛptyabhāve dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*56] '<s>Santaḥ</s>' means those steadfast in the devotion of servitude (<s>dāsya-bhakti</s>) — this is the illustration for the absence of satiation. |

body.text: animiṣantībhyām animīlantībhyāṃ dṛgbhyām āpītam api samyag dṛṣṭam api punaḥ punar juṣāṇā nātṛpyat ||BhPC_10,32.7||
body.translated_text: 'With unblinking' — with eyes that do not close; 'though fully drunk in (<s>āpītam</s>)' means though fully seen; savoring [it] again and again, she was not satiated. ||BhPC_10,32.7||

children.text: taṃ kācin netrarandhreṇa hṛdi kṛtya nimīlya ca /
children.translated_text: One [<s>gopī</s>], drawing him in through the aperture of her eyes into her heart, and closing [her eyes],
with body thrilling with horripilation, sat embracing [him within], immersed in bliss like a <s>yogī</s>. //

body.text: [*57] yogīvety antaḥsphūrtau dṛṣṭāntaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*57] 'Like a <s>yogī</s>' — this is the illustration for the internal manifestation [of the beloved]. |

body.text: hṛdi kṛtya hṛdayaṃ nītvety arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,32.8||
body.translated_text: 'Having placed in the heart (<s>hṛdi kṛtya</s>)' means having brought [him] into the heart: this is the meaning. ||BhPC_10,32.8||

children.translated_text: All of them, filled with the supreme joy of beholding <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: jahur virahajaṃ tāpaṃ prājñaṃ prāpya yathā janāḥ //
children.translated_text: abandoned their torment born of separation, as people [abandon suffering] upon attaining the Omniscient One. //

body.text: prājñaṃ īśvaraṃ prāpya yathā mumukṣavo janāḥ | yadvā prājñaṃ brahmajñaṃ prāpya yathā saṃsāriṇaḥ | yadvā prājñaṃ sauṣuptaṃ[*58] prāpya yathā viśvataijasāvasthā jīvāḥ ||BhPC_10,32.9||
body.translated_text: '<s>Prājñam</s>' means the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) — as seekers of liberation (<s>mumukṣavaḥ</s>) [abandon suffering] upon attaining Him. Alternatively, '<s>prājñam</s>' means one who knows <s>Brahman</s> — as worldly beings (<s>saṃsāriṇaḥ</s>) [abandon suffering] upon attaining such a knower. Or, '<s>prājñam</s>' means the witness of deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>) — as the individual souls in the waking (<s>viśva</s>) and dream (<s>taijasa</s>) states [abandon suffering upon attaining that state]. ||BhPC_10,32.9||

body.text: [*58] sauṣuptaṃ suṣuptisākṣiṇam ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*58] '<s>Sauṣuptam</s>' means 'the witness of deep sleep (<s>suṣupti</s>)': this is the meaning. |

children.translated_text: <s>Bhagavān Acyuta</s>, surrounded by those [<s>gopīs</s>] whose grief had been dispelled,
shone forth exceedingly, O dear one, as the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣa</s>) [shines] with his powers (<s>śaktis</s>). //

body.text: puruṣaḥ paramātmā śaktibhiḥ sattvādibhir yathā | yadvā upāsakaḥ puruṣo jñānabalavīryādibhiḥ | yadvā puruṣo 'nuśāyī prakṛtyādyupādhibhir vṛto yathā 'dhikaṃ virocate tadvat ||BhPC_10,32.10||
body.translated_text: '<s>Puruṣa</s>' means the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātmā</s>), with powers (<s>śaktis</s>) such as <s>sattva</s> and the rest. Alternatively, the worshipping person (<s>upāsaka puruṣa</s>) [shines] with knowledge, strength, valor, and the like. Or, '<s>Puruṣa</s>' the indwelling Self (<s>anuśāyī</s>), surrounded by limiting adjuncts (<s>upādhis</s>) such as <s>Prakṛti</s> — just as He shines exceedingly, so too [did <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> shine]. ||BhPC_10,32.10||

children.text: tāḥ samādāya kālindyā nirviśya[*59] pulinaṃ vibhuḥ /
children.translated_text: Taking them along, the all-pervading Lord entered the sandy bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>),
[a place] with bees [attracted by] the fragrant breeze from blossoming <s>kunda</s> and <s>mandāra</s> flowers. //

body.text: [*59] nirviśya adhiṣṭhāya |
body.translated_text: [*59] '<s>Nirviśya</s>' means having entered, having settled upon. |

body.text: vikasatkundamandāraiḥ surabhir yo 'nilas tasmāt ṣaṭpadā yasmiṃs tat ||BhPC_10,32.11||
body.translated_text: The breeze is fragrant (<s>surabhi</s>) from the blossoming <s>kunda</s> and <s>mandāra</s> [flowers]; because of that [fragrant breeze], bees (<s>ṣaṭpada</s>) are there — [a place] possessing such [bees]. ||BhPC_10,32.11||

children.translated_text: [A place] auspicious, its nocturnal darkness dispelled by the profusion of rays of the autumn moon,
with soft sand spread by the wave-like hands of the <s>Kālindī</s> [river]. //

body.text: śaraccandrāṃśūnāṃ sandohaiḥ samūhair dhvastaṃ doṣātamo rātrigataṃ tamo yasmiṃs tat | ataḥ śivaṃ sukhakaram | hastarūpais taralais taraṅgair ācitā āstṛtā komalā vālukā yasmin | evaṃbhūtaṃ pulinaṃ tāḥ samādāya nirviśya tābhir vṛto 'dhikaṃ vyarocateti pūrveṇānvayaḥ ||BhPC_10,32.12||
body.translated_text: 'By the clusters (<s>sandoha</s>) of autumn moonbeams, the nocturnal darkness (<s>doṣātamas</s>) is dispelled (<s>dhvasta</s>)' — therefore it is '<s>śivam</s>' (auspicious, pleasant). 'With its hand-like rippling waves (<s>tarala</s>), the soft sand (<s>komalā vālukā</s>) is spread (<s>ācitā</s>).' Such a sandy bank — taking them along and entering it, surrounded by them, He shone exceedingly: this is the syntactical connection with the previous [verse]. ||BhPC_10,32.12||

children.translated_text: Their heart-agonies dispelled by the joy of seeing him, they attained the fulfillment of their desires, just as the <s>Śrutis</s> (scriptures) [attain their goal].

children.text: svair uttarīyaiḥ kucakuṅkumāṅkitair acīk pann āsanam ātmabandhave //
children.translated_text: With their own upper garments marked with breast-saffron stains, they prepared a seat for their beloved friend. //

body.text: tāś ca manorathānām antaṃ yayuḥ pūrṇakāmā babhūvuḥ | śrutayo yatheti | ayam arthaḥ-yathā karmakāṇḍe śrutayaḥ parameśvaram apaśyantyas tat tatkāmānubandhair apūrṇā iva bhavanti, jñānakāṇḍe tu parameśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā tadāhlādapūrṇāḥ kāmānubandhaṃ jahati tadvad iti | āptakāmā api premṇā tam abhajann ity āha-svair iti | acīk pan racayāmāsuḥ | ātmabandhave 'ntaryāmiṇe ||BhPC_10,32.13||
body.translated_text: And they attained the end of [their] desires — they became fully satisfied. 'Like the <s>Śrutis</s>' — the meaning is as follows: just as in the <s>Karma-kāṇḍa</s> (ritual section), the <s>Śrutis</s>, not seeing the Supreme Lord, remain as if unfulfilled with their various desire-connections, but in the <s>Jñāna-kāṇḍa</s> (knowledge section), upon seeing the Supreme Lord, they abandon the connection with desires, being filled with the joy of that [vision] — so too [did the <s>gopīs</s>]. Though they had already attained their desires, [the text] says they worshipped him out of love — with '<s>svaiḥ</s>' etc. '<s>Acīkṛpan</s>' means 'they prepared, they arranged.' '<s>Ātma-bandhave</s>' means 'for the inner controller (<s>antaryāmin</s>).' ||BhPC_10,32.13||

children.translated_text: There, having sat down, that <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Lord, upon a seat fashioned within the hearts of the masters of <s>yoga</s> (<s>yogeśvaras</s>),
shone resplendent amidst the assembly of <s>gopīs</s>, honored [by them], bearing a form that was the sole abode of the beauty of the three worlds. //

body.text:
[*60] hṛdikalpitāsanaḥ ity aluksamāsaḥ |
[*61] arcitas tāmbūlanarmasmitādinā satkṛtaḥ |
body.translated_text:
[*60] '<s>Hṛdi-kalpitāsanaḥ</s>' — this is an <s>aluk-samāsa</s> (a compound retaining the case ending). |
[*61] '<s>Arcitaḥ</s>' means honored with <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel), playful words, smiles, and so forth. |

body.text: gopīsabhāgatas tābhiḥ saṃmānitaḥ san cakāsa śuśubhe | trailokye yā lakṣmīḥ śobhā tasyā ekam eva padaṃ sthānaṃ tadvapur dadhad darśayan ||BhPC_10,32.14||
body.translated_text: Having entered the assembly of the <s>gopīs</s>, honored by them, He shone forth (<s>cakāsa</s>), He was resplendent. Bearing — that is, displaying — a form that was the sole abode (<s>padam</s>) of the beauty (<s>lakṣmī</s>) of the three worlds. ||BhPC_10,32.14||

children.translated_text: Having honored him, the inflamer of <s>Anaṅga</s> (bodiless Cupid), with playful, laughing glances and the coquetry of [their] brows,
and with the touch of [placing] his feet and hands upon their laps, praising [him], slightly angered, they spoke. //

body.text: [*62] babhāṣire vakṣyamāṇaṃ papracchur iti śeṣaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*62] '<s>Babhāṣire</s>' — the remainder is: 'they asked what is about to be stated.' |

body.text: sahāsalīlekṣaṇena vibhramo vilāso yasyāṃ tayā bhruvopalakṣitāḥ | saṃsparśanena saṃmardanena ||BhPC_10,32.15||
body.translated_text: 'Playful, laughing glances (<s>sahāsa-līlekṣaṇa</s>)' — the coquettish play (<s>vibhrama</s>, <s>vilāsa</s>) expressed through the brows, which are indicated [thereby]. 'By touching (<s>saṃsparśana</s>)' means by pressing, caressing. ||BhPC_10,32.15||

children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s> said:
Some reciprocate those who worship them; some do the reverse of this;

children.text: nobhayāṃś[*63] ca bhajanty eka etan no brūhi sādhu bhoḥ //
children.translated_text: and some worship neither [type] — O noble one, please explain this to us properly! //

body.text: [*63] "nobhayāś ca bhajanty anye" iti pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*63] Another reading is: '<s>nobhayāś ca bhajanty anye</s>' ('and others worship neither'). |

body.text: tatra bhagavato 'kṛtajñatāṃ tadvacanenaivāpādayitukāmā gūḍhābhiprāyā lokavṛttāntam iva pṛcchanti-bhajata iti | bhajataḥ prāṇinaḥ | anu anantaraṃ | kecit tadbhajanānusāreṇa bhajanti | kecid etad viparyayaṃ yathā bhavati tathā | tadbhajanān apekṣam abhajato 'pi bhajanti | anye tu nobhayān[*64] iti ||BhPC_10,32.16||
body.translated_text: There, wishing to establish <s>Bhagavān's</s> ingratitude through his own words, with hidden intent, they ask as if inquiring about worldly affairs — '<s>bhajataḥ</s>' etc. '<s>Bhajataḥ</s>' means living beings. '<s>Anu</s>' means 'subsequently.' Some reciprocate by worshipping in accordance with that person's worship [of them]. Some [do] the reverse of this — that is, even without being worshipped by them, they worship [others] independently. 'Others' — '<s>nobhayān</s>' etc. ||BhPC_10,32.16||

body.text: [*64] ubhayān bhajataḥ abhajataś ca |
body.translated_text: [*64] '<s>Ubhayān</s>' — both those who worship and those who do not worship. |

children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Bhagavān</s> said:

children.text: mitho bhajanti ye sakhyaḥ svārthaikāntodyamā hi te /
children.translated_text: Those who mutually worship [each other], O friends — they are solely engaged in striving for their own interest.

children.text: na tatra sauhṛdaṃ dharmaḥ svārthārthaṃ tad dhi nānyathā[*65] //
children.translated_text: In that there is neither true friendship nor <s>dharma</s> (righteousness); it is only for self-interest, and not otherwise. //

body.text: [*65] nānyathā parārtham ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*65] 'Not otherwise' — meaning: not for the sake of another. |

body.text: viditābhiprāya uttaram āha-mitha iti | he sakhyaḥ, upakārapratyupakāratayā ye mitho bhajanti te 'nyaṃ na bhajanti kiṃ tv ātmānam eva | kutaḥ | hi yasmāt svārtha[*66] evaikānta udyamo yeṣāṃ te | tatra ca na[*67] sauhṛdam ato na sukhaṃ, na ca dharmo dṛṣṭoddeśād gomahiṣyādibhajanavad ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,32.17||
body.translated_text: Knowing their intent, He gives the answer — '<s>mithaḥ</s>' etc. O friends (<s>sakhyaḥ</s>), those who worship each other (<s>mithaḥ</s>) in the manner of favor and counter-favor — they do not worship anyone else; rather, [they worship] only themselves. Why? Because (<s>hi</s>) they are those whose sole (<s>ekānta</s>) endeavor (<s>udyama</s>) is for their own interest (<s>svārtha</s>). And in that, there is no true affection (<s>sauhṛda</s>), hence no happiness; nor is there <s>dharma</s> — just like tending cows and buffaloes for visible gain: this is the meaning. ||BhPC_10,32.17||

body.text:
[*66] svārthe svīye dṛṣṭaphale |
[*67] na sauhṛdaṃ kaitavamayatvāt |
body.translated_text:
[*66] '<s>Svārthe</s>' — in one's own visible gain. |
[*67] 'No true affection (<s>sauhṛdam</s>)' — because it is deceitful (<s>kaitava-maya</s>). |

children.text: bhajanty abhajato ye vai karuṇāḥ pitaro yathā /
children.translated_text: Those who serve those who do not serve [them in return], being compassionate, like parents —
that is blameless <s>dharma</s> and true friendship, O slender-waisted ones! // <s>BhP</s> 10.32.18

body.text: [*68] nirapavādo nirbādhaḥ | idaṃ sauhṛdasyāpi viśeṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: [*68] 'Blameless' (<s>nirapavāda</s>) means unobstructed. This is also a qualifier of 'friendship' (<s>sauhṛda</s>).

body.text: ye tv abhajato bhajanti te dvividhāḥ | karuṇāḥ snigdhāś ca | tatra tu yathākramaṃ dharmakāmau bhavata ity āha-bhajanty abhajata iti ||BhPC_10,32.18||
body.translated_text: Those who serve those who do not serve [them] are of two kinds: the compassionate and the affectionate. Among these, in order, <s>dharma</s> and <s>kāma</s> (desire) are [the respective motives] — thus he says with 'they serve those who do not serve' etc. ||BhPC_10,32.18||

children.text: bhajato 'pi na vai kecid bhajanty abhajataḥ kutaḥ /
children.translated_text: Some do not serve even those who serve [them] — how then [would they serve] those who do not serve?
[They are] self-delighting, fulfilled in desires, ungrateful, and treacherous to benefactors. //

body.text: tṛtīyapraśnottaraṃ bhajato 'pīti | ayam arthaḥ-te tu caturvidhāḥ | eke ātmārāmā aparāgdṛśaḥ, kecid āptakāmā viṣayadarśino 'pi pūrṇakāmatvena bhogecchārahitāḥ, anye 'kṛtajñā mūḍhāḥ, anye tu gurudruho 'tikaṭhināḥ "sa pitā yas tu poṣakaḥ" iti nyāyād upakartā gurutulyas tasmai druhyantīti tathā te ||BhPC_10,32.19||
body.translated_text: The answer to the third question — 'even those who serve' etc. The meaning is this: they are of four kinds. Some are <s>ātmārāma</s> (self-delighting), seeing without passion; some are <s>āptakāma</s> (fulfilled in desires), even though seeing sense objects, being free from desire for enjoyment due to completeness of desire; others are <s>akṛtajña</s> (ungrateful), i.e., deluded; and yet others are <s>gurudruha</s> (treacherous to benefactors), i.e., exceedingly hard-hearted — by the maxim 'he is a father who nourishes,' a benefactor is equal to a <s>guru</s>, and they betray him — thus they are so. ||BhPC_10,32.19||

children.text: nāhaṃ tu sakhyo bhajato 'pi jantūn bhajāmy amīṣām anuvṛttivṛttaye /
children.translated_text: But I, O friends, do not serve the beings who serve me, [and this is] in order to maintain their continued devotion,

children.text: yathādhano labdhadhane vinaṣṭe taccintayānyan nibhṛto na veda //
children.translated_text: just as a poor man who has obtained wealth and then lost it, absorbed in thought of that alone, knows nothing else. //

body.text: atra caramakoṭigatam ātmānaṃ matvā, akṣisaṃkocaiḥ parasparaṃ gūḍhasmitamukhīs tā dṛṣṭvā āha-nāhaṃ tv iti | he sakhyaḥ, ahaṃ teṣāṃ madhye na ko 'pi, kiṃ tu paramakāruṇikaḥ paramasuhṛc ca | katham | amīṣāṃ bhajatām anuvṛttivṛtaye nirantaradhyānapravṛttyarthaṃ tān na bhajāmi | etat sadṛṣṭāntam āha-yatheti | tasya dhanasyaiva cintayā nibhṛtaḥ pūrṇaḥ | vyāpta iti yāvat | anyat kṣutpipāsādy api na veda ||BhPC_10,32.20||
body.translated_text: Here, considering Himself to have reached the final extreme [of those who do not reciprocate], and seeing them with half-closed eyes, exchanging secret smiles — He says 'But I' etc. O friends, among those [four types] I am not any one; rather, I am supremely compassionate and the supreme friend. How so? I do not serve those who serve Me, for the purpose of maintaining their continued devotion (<s>anuvṛtti</s>), i.e., for the sake of uninterrupted meditation. He illustrates this with an example — 'just as' etc. Absorbed (<s>nibhṛta</s>) means filled, pervaded, with the thought of that very wealth alone. He does not know anything else, not even hunger and thirst etc. ||BhPC_10,32.20||

children.text: evaṃ madarthojjhitalokavedasvānāṃ hi vo mayy anuvṛttaye 'balāḥ /
children.translated_text: Thus, O women, you who have abandoned worldly ties, Vedic duties, and kinsmen for My sake,

children.text: mayā parokṣaṃ bhajatā tirohitaṃ māsūyituṃ mārhatha tat priyaṃ priyāḥ //
children.translated_text: I who served you while hidden from sight — you should not harbor resentment toward Me. That is dear [to Me], O beloved ones! //

body.text: evaṃ madarthojjhitalokavedasvānāṃ madarthe ujjhito loko yuktāyuktāpratīkṣaṇāt, vedaś ca dharmādharmāpratīkṣaṇāt, svā jñātayaś ca snehatyāgāt yābhis tāsāṃ vo yuṣmākaṃ parokṣam adarśanaṃ yathā bhavati tathā bhajatā yuṣmat premālāpān śṛṇvataiva tirohitam antardhānena sthitam | tat tasmāt he abalā he priyāḥ, mā mām[*69] asūyituṃ doṣāropeṇa draṣṭuṃ yūyaṃ mārhatha na yogyāḥ stha ||BhPC_10,32.21||
body.translated_text: 'Who have abandoned worldly ties, Vedic duties, and kinsmen for My sake' — 'worldly ties' (<s>loka</s>) [are abandoned] through disregard for what is proper and improper; 'Vedic duties' (<s>veda</s>) through disregard for <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>; 'kinsmen' (<s>sva</s>) through abandoning affection. The 'hiddenness' (<s>parokṣam</s>), i.e., invisibility, which occurred while I was serving you — while hearing your loving words — [I was] standing hidden through concealment. Therefore, O women, O beloved ones, you should not be fit to impute fault to Me — you are not justified [in resentment]. ||BhPC_10,32.21||

body.text: [*69] yadvā mādvayaṃ niṣedhe | tathāpi priyaṃ mallakṣaṇam asūyituṃ mārhatheti mā | api tu mayā dattaduḥkhatvād athaiveti |
body.translated_text: [*69] Alternatively, the two instances of '<s>mā</s>' are both prohibitive. Even so, the meaning is: '[it is] dear' — a characteristic of Me — 'do not impute fault' — this is the [meaning of] '<s>mā</s>.' But rather, because I am the giver of suffering — [the intent is] 'even so' etc.

children.text: na pāraye 'haṃ niravadyasaṃyujāṃ svasādhukṛtyaṃ vibudhāyuṣāpi vaḥ /
children.translated_text: I am unable to repay even in a lifetime of the gods the good service of you whose union is blameless.

children.text: yā mābhajan durjaragehaśṛṅkhalāḥ[*70] saṃvṛścya tad vaḥ pratiyātu sādhunā //
children.translated_text: You who have broken the unbreakable chains of household [bondage] to serve Me — may your own good deed be your recompense! //

body.text: [*70] "śṛṅkhalām" iti vā pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*70] The reading '<s>śṛṅkhalām</s>' [in the singular] is also [found].

body.text: āstām idaṃ, paramarthaṃ tu śṛṇutety āha-neti | niravadyā saṃyuk saṃyogo yāsāṃ tāsāṃ vo vibudhānām[*71] āyuṣāpi cirakāle 'pi svīyaṃ sādhu kṛtyaṃ pratyupakāraṃ kartuṃ na pāraye na śaknomi | kathaṃ bhūtānām | yā bhavatyo durjarā ajarā yā gehaśṛṅkhalās tāḥ saṃvṛścya niḥśeṣaṃ chittvā mā mām abhajaṃs tāsām | maccittaṃ tu bahuṣu premayuktatayā naikaniṣṭham | tasmād vo yuṣmākam eva sādhunā sādhukṛtyena tat yuṣmat sādhu kṛtyaṃ pratiyātu pratikṛtaṃ bhavatu | yuṣmat sauśīlyenaiva mamānṛṇyaṃ, na tu matkṛtapratyupakāreṇety arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,32.22||
body.translated_text: Let this be — but hear the ultimate truth — thus He says 'I am unable' etc. I am unable, even in a lifetime of the gods — i.e., even over a long time — to perform My own proper reciprocation toward you whose union (<s>saṃyuj</s>) is blameless (<s>niravadya</s>). What kind of women? You who have completely severed (<s>saṃvṛścya</s>) the unbreakable (<s>durjara</s>) chains of household [life] and have served Me. But My mind, being endowed with love toward many, is not fixed on one alone. Therefore, may your good deed be your recompense (<s>pratiyātu</s>) for your own good conduct. Your own graciousness alone frees Me from debt, not any reciprocal service performed by Me — this is the meaning. ||BhPC_10,32.22||

body.text: [*71] yadvā vigato budho gaṇanābhijño yasmāt tenānantenāyuṣāpi |
body.translated_text: [*71] Alternatively, '<s>vibudha</s>' [means] one devoid of '<s>budha</s>' (the knower of calculation), i.e., by a lifetime that is incalculable — even by that infinite [span].

body.text: iti śrīmadbhāgavate mahāpurāṇe daśamaskandhe pūrvārdhe bhāvārthadīpikāyāṃ ṭīkāyāṃ dvātriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ **32**
body.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the tenth book, first half, in the commentary called <s>Bhāvārthadīpikā</s>, the thirty-second chapter. **32**

children.translated_text: [Chapter 33:] Then <s>Hari</s>, having entered the circle of <s>gopīs</s>,
delighted those beloved ones with sports on the riverbank and in the forest. // 1 //
<s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:

children.text: itthaṃ bhagavato gopyaḥ śrutvā vācaḥ supeśalāḥ[*72] /
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>gopīs</s>, having heard the charming words of <s>Bhagavān</s>,
gave up the anguish born of separation, their desires fulfilled by the touch of His limbs. //

body.text: [*72] supeśalā manoharāḥ |
body.translated_text: [*72] '<s>Supeśalā</s>' means captivating to the heart.

body.text: tat tadā aṅga he rājan, yadvā tasya bhagavato 'ṅgena vapuṣā karacaraṇādyavayavair vopacitāḥ samṛddhā āśiṣo yāsāṃ[*73] tāḥ ||BhPC_10,33.1||
body.translated_text: '<s>Tat</s>' — then; or, O king (<s>aṅga</s>), '<s>tat</s>' means of that <s>Bhagavān</s> — by His body (<s>aṅga</s>), i.e., by the limbs such as hands and feet etc. — their desires were enriched (<s>upacitāḥ</s>), i.e., fulfilled. ||BhPC_10,33.1||

body.text: [*73] yadvā tāsāṃ gopīnām aṅgair upacitā āśiṣo yasya |
body.translated_text: [*73] Alternatively, the desires of those <s>gopīs</s> were enriched by His limbs.

children.translated_text: There <s>Govinda</s> began the <s>Rāsa</s> dance with the devoted
jewels among women, joyful, with arms linked to one another. //

body.text: rāsakrīḍāṃ rāso[*74] nāma bahunartakīyukto nṛtyaviśeṣas tāṃ krīḍām | anyonyam ābaddhāḥ saṃgrathitā bāhavo yais taiḥ saha ||BhPC_10,33.2||
body.translated_text: The '<s>Rāsa</s> dance' (<s>rāsakrīḍā</s>) — '<s>rāsa</s>' is a special type of dance involving many female dancers; that was the sport. 'With arms linked to one another' — with arms mutually interlaced. ||BhPC_10,33.2||

body.text: [*74] "natair gṛhītakaṇṭhānām anyonyāttakaraśriyam / nartakīnāṃ bhaved rāso maṇḍalībhūya nartanam //" iti rāsalakṣaṇam |
body.translated_text: [*74] 'Dancing in a circle by dancers whose necks are held [by partners] and whose hand-beauty is mutually grasped — that is the definition of <s>Rāsa</s>.'

children.translated_text: The <s>Rāsa</s> festival commenced, adorned by the circle of <s>gopīs</s>,

children.text: yogeśvareṇa kṛṣṇena[*75] tāsāṃ madhye dvayor dvayoḥ /
children.translated_text: [with] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the lord of <s>yoga</s>, [who had] entered between every two [<s>gopīs</s>],
holding the necks of those women [who each thought Him] near themselves. //

body.text: [*75] kṛṣṇena nimittena saṃpravṛttaḥ | yadvāntarbhāvitaṇyarthaḥ | kṛṣṇena samyak pravṛtta ity arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*75] 'By <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — [the festival] commenced by that cause. Alternatively, with the causative sense implicit — 'well commenced by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' is the meaning.

body.text: tatsāhityam abhinayena darśayati-rāsotsava ity akṣaracatuṣṭayādhikena sārdhena | tāsāṃ maṇḍalarūpeṇāvasthitānāṃ dvayor dvayor madhye praviṣṭena tenaiva kaṇṭhe gṛhītānām ubhayata āliṅgitānām | kathaṃbhūtena | yaṃ sarvāḥ striyaḥ svanikaṭaṃ mām evāśliṣṭavān iti manyeraṃs tena etad arthaṃ dvayor dvayor madhye praviṣṭenety arthaḥ | nanv ekasya kathaṃ tathā praveśaḥ, sarvasannihitatve vā kutaḥ svaikanikaṭatvābhimānas tāsām ity ata uktaṃ-yogeśvareṇeti | acintyaśaktinety arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.3||
body.translated_text: He shows this accompaniment through dramatic description — 'The <s>Rāsa</s> festival' etc., in four and a half feet of verse. Having entered between every two of those [<s>gopīs</s>] who stood in a circular formation, He who held their necks, i.e., embraced them from both sides. Of what nature? Such that all the women thought 'He has embraced me alone, near me alone' — for this purpose He entered between every two. But how can one [person] enter thus [between every pair]? And if present near all simultaneously, how could they each have the conviction of His exclusive proximity? — therefore it is said 'the lord of <s>yoga</s>' — meaning [He possesses] inconceivable power. ||BhPC_10,33.3||

children.translated_text: At that [moment], the sky was filled with hundreds of celestial chariots
of the gods with their wives, whose minds were seized by eager curiosity. //

body.text: tāvat tatkṣaṇam evautsukyavyāptamanasāṃ sastrīkāṇāṃ devānāṃ vimānaśataiḥ saṅkulaṃ saṅkīrṇaṃ nabho babhūva ||BhPC_10,33.4||
body.translated_text: At that very moment, the sky became crowded with hundreds of chariots of the gods accompanied by their wives, whose minds were pervaded by eager curiosity. ||BhPC_10,33.4||

children.translated_text: Then kettledrums resounded and showers of flowers fell;
the lords of the <s>Gandharvas</s> with their wives sang His spotless glory. //

body.text: tat tasya bhagavataḥ śrīkṛṣṇasyāmalaṃ nirmalaṃ yaśo jagur iti ||BhPC_10,33.5||
body.translated_text: '<s>Tat</s>' — of that <s>Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> — they sang the spotless (<s>amala</s>), i.e., pure, glory. ||BhPC_10,33.5||

children.translated_text: Of the bracelets, anklets, and tinkling bells of the women
who were with their beloved, there arose a tumultuous sound in the <s>Rāsa</s> circle. //

body.text: sapriyāṇāṃ kṛṣṇasahitānām | tumulaḥ saṅkīrṇaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.6||
body.translated_text: 'With their beloved' (<s>sapriyāṇām</s>) means accompanied by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. 'Tumultuous' (<s>tumula</s>) means dense, intermingled. ||BhPC_10,33.6||

children.translated_text: There, amidst them, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the son of <s>Devakī</s>, shone exceedingly
like a great emerald in the midst of golden gems. //

body.text: mahāmarakato nīlamaṇir iva haimānāṃ maṇīnāṃ madhye madhye tābhiḥ svarṇavarṇābhir āśliṣṭābhiḥ śuśubhe | gopīdṛṣṭyabhiprāyeṇa vā vinaiva madhyapadāvṛttim ekavacanam ||BhPC_10,33.7||
body.translated_text: Like a great emerald (<s>mahāmarakata</s>), i.e., a sapphire, amidst golden gems — in their midst, embraced by those golden-complexioned [<s>gopīs</s>], He shone resplendently. Or, from the viewpoint of the <s>gopīs</s>' perception, the singular 'midst' [is used] without the medial word-repetition [indicating each one thought He was in her midst alone]. ||BhPC_10,33.7||

children.translated_text: With footsteps, with arm-movements, with smiling glances and brow-play,
with bending waists, with swaying breast-cloths, with earrings dangling on their cheeks,
with perspiring faces, with loosening braids and girdle-knots, the wives of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: gāyantyas taṃ taḍita iva tā meghacakre virejuḥ //
children.translated_text: singing of Him, shone like flashes of lightning in a circle of clouds. //

body.text: sa yathā tābhiḥ śuśubhe, tathā tā api tena virejur ity āha-pādanyāsair iti | bhujavidhutibhiḥ karacālanair bhajyamānair madhyaiś caladbhiḥ kucaiś ca paṭaiś ca | gaṇḍalolair gaṇḍeṣu cañcalaiḥ | svidyan mukhyaḥ svidyanti svedam udgiranti mukhāni yāsāṃ tāḥ | kabareṣu raśanāsu ca granthayo dṛḍhā yāsām | yadvā teṣu tāsu cāgranthayaḥ, śithilagranthaya ity arthaḥ | tatra nānāmūrtiḥ kṛṣṇo meghacakram iva, tās tu bahuvidhās taḍita iva svedas tuṣāra iva, gītaṃ garjitam eveti yathāsaṃbhavamūhyam ||BhPC_10,33.8||
body.translated_text: Just as He shone resplendently among them, so too they shone through Him — thus he says 'With footsteps' etc. 'Arm-movements' (<s>bhujavidhuti</s>) means wavings of the hands. 'Bending waists' (<s>bhajyan madhyaiḥ</s>) [means] with waists that were bending, and with swaying breast-cloths. 'Dangling on cheeks' (<s>gaṇḍalola</s>) means swinging upon the cheeks. 'With perspiring faces' (<s>svidyanmukhyaḥ</s>) — those whose faces exude perspiration. 'With loosening braids and girdle-knots' (<s>kabararaśanāgranthayaḥ</s>) — those whose knots in their braids and girdles [were loosened]. Or, whose knots in those [braids and girdles] were undone — meaning with loosened knots. In this [simile], <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in His manifold forms is like a mass of clouds; they, being of many kinds, are like lightning; the perspiration is like frost; and the singing is like thunder — thus the correspondence should be understood as fitting. ||BhPC_10,33.8||

children.translated_text: They sang aloud while dancing, with reddened throats, dear to <s>Rati</s> (the goddess of love),
delighted by the touch of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, by whose song this [entire universe] was pervaded. //

body.text: [*76] nṛtyamānā iti nṛtyakāle 'pi gānaṃ śānajārṣaḥ | yadvā tācchīlyād auśānac | yadvā nṛtyena mānaḥ kṛṣṇakṛto yāsām |
body.translated_text: [*76] 'Dancing' — even at the time of dance, singing [is indicated]; the <s>śānac</s> suffix is Vedic usage. Or, from the habitual sense, the <s>auśānac</s> [suffix applies]. Or, those whose honor (<s>māna</s>) was made by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> through dance.

body.text: nṛtyamānā nṛtyantyaḥ | raktakaṇṭhyo nānārāgair anurañjitakaṇṭhyaḥ | kṛṣṇasyābhimarśena saṃsparśena muditāḥ | idaṃ viśvam ||BhPC_10,33.9||
body.translated_text: 'Dancing' means those who are dancing. 'With reddened throats' means with throats colored by various musical modes (<s>rāga</s>). 'Delighted by the touch (<s>abhimarśa</s>), the contact of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.' 'This' means the universe. ||BhPC_10,33.9||

children.translated_text: One <s>gopī</s>, together with <s>Mukunda</s>, sang unmixed melodic patterns of the musical notes,

children.text: unninye pūjitā tena prīyatā sādhu sādhv iti /
children.translated_text: and was praised by Him who was pleased, [saying] 'Excellent! Excellent!'

children.text: tad eva dhruvam unninye tasyai mānaṃ ca bahv adāt //
children.translated_text: She then sang the very same [melody] as a <s>dhruva</s> (a fixed refrain), and He bestowed upon her great honor. //

body.text: mukundena saha svarajātīḥ ṣaḍjādisvarālāpagatīḥ | amiśritāḥ kṛṣṇonnītābhir asaṅkīrṇāḥ | prīyamāṇena saṃmānitā tajjāty unnayanam eva dhruvaṃ dhruvākhyaṃ tālaviśeṣaṃ kṛtvā unninye unnītavatī ||BhPC_10,33.10||
body.translated_text: 'Melodic patterns of the notes' means the sequences of notes beginning with <s>ṣaḍja</s> and other <s>svaras</s>. 'Unmixed' means not intermingled with those raised by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Honored by [Him] who was pleased, she performed the very raising of that melodic type as a <s>dhruva</s>, a particular rhythmic pattern (<s>tālaviśeṣa</s>), and sang it forth. ||BhPC_10,33.10||

children.translated_text: One <s>gopī</s>, fatigued from the <s>Rāsa</s> dance, grasped the shoulder of the mace-bearer (<s>Gadābhṛt</s>)
who stood beside her, with her arm, her bracelets and jasmine garlands slipping. //

body.text: evaṃ nṛtyagītādinā śrīkṛṣṇasaṃmānitānāṃ tāsām atiprītivilasitaṃ vṛttam āha-kācid iti | ślathanti valayāni mallikāś ca yasyāḥ sā ||BhPC_10,33.11||
body.translated_text: Thus, describing the delightful amorous conduct of those [<s>gopīs</s>] who had been honored by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> through dance, song, and the like, he says 'One <s>gopī</s>...' She whose bracelets and jasmine flowers are slipping — such is she. ||BhPC_10,33.11||

children.translated_text: There, [she smelled] the arm of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> resting on her shoulder, fragrant as a blue lotus,
anointed with sandalwood, and smelling it, with hair standing on end, she kissed it. //

body.text: utpalasya saurabhaṃ yasya taṃ bāhum ||BhPC_10,33.12||
body.translated_text: That arm which has the fragrance of a lotus — [she smelled] that arm. ||BhPC_10,33.12||

children.translated_text: The cheek of a certain [<s>gopī</s>], adorned by the luster of earrings set swinging by her dance,
as she pressed her cheek to [His] cheek, He gave her the chewed betel (<s>tāmbūla</s>). //

body.text: nāṭyena nṛtyena vikṣiptayoś cañcalayoḥ kuṇḍalayos[*77] tviṣeṇa tviṣā maṇḍitaṃ gaṇḍaṃ kapolaṃ tathābhūte svagaṇḍe saṃdadhatyāḥ saṃyojayantyāḥ ||BhPC_10,33.13||
body.translated_text: 'Set swinging by dance' means the two earrings made restless by dancing; 'adorned by their luster' means adorned by the radiance of those [earrings]; 'cheek' means the temple. 'To her who was joining' means to her who was pressing her own cheek [against His] in that manner. ||BhPC_10,33.13||

body.text: [*77] nṛtyena vikṣipte cañcale kuṇḍale ca svābhāvikī gaṇḍatviṭ ca tatsamāhāras tviṣaṃ tena maṇḍitam iti | "dvandvāc cudaṣahāntāt" iti ṭac |
body.translated_text: [*77] The two earrings set swinging, made restless by dance, and the natural luster of the cheeks — their aggregate; 'adorned by that luster.' The <s>ṭac</s> suffix [applies] by the rule 'from <s>dvandva</s> compounds ending in <s>cu</s> etc.'

children.translated_text: One [<s>gopī</s>] was dancing and singing, her anklets and girdle tinkling,
and being fatigued, she placed the auspicious lotus-hand of <s>Acyuta</s> who stood beside her upon her breasts. //

body.text: kūjatī nūpure mekhalā ca yasyāḥ sā ||BhPC_10,33.14||
body.translated_text: She whose anklets and girdle tinkle — such is she. ||BhPC_10,33.14||

children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s>, having obtained <s>Acyuta</s> as their beloved, the exclusive darling of <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>),
embracing His neck, sporting with Him through His arms, singing of Him. //

body.text: evam anyā api gopyo yathā yathaṃ nānāvibhramair vijahrur ity āha-gopya iti ||BhPC_10,33.15||
body.translated_text: Thus the other <s>gopīs</s> also sported in various ways with various amorous gestures — he says this with '<s>gopīs</s>.' ||BhPC_10,33.15||

children.translated_text: With the beauty of faces [adorned] with lotuses at the ears, curling locks, lovely cheeks, and drops of perspiration, with the music of bracelets, anklets, and bells as instruments,

children.text: gopyaḥ samaṃ bhagavatā nanṛtuḥ svakeśasrastasrajo bhramaragāyakarāsagoṣṭhyām //
children.translated_text: the <s>gopīs</s> danced together with the Lord in the <s>Rāsa</s> assembly where bees served as singers, their garlands having fallen from their hair. //

body.text: tatra vādakeṣu gāyakeṣu gandharvakinnarādiṣu rasāveśena muhyatsu cānyām eva vādyādi-sampattiṃ darśayan rāsasaṃbhramam āha-karṇotpalair iti | karṇotpalaiś cālakaviṭaṅkair alakālaṅkṛtaiḥ kapolaiś ca gharmaiś ca vaktreṣu śrīḥ śobhā yāsāṃ tāḥ | ghoṣāḥ kiṅkiṇyaḥ | valayanūpuraghoṣair vādyair vāditraiḥ svakeśebhyaḥ srastāḥ srajo yāsāṃ tāḥ | etena tālagatisaṃtuṣṭāḥ keśāḥ saśiraḥkampaṃ pādeṣu puṣpavṛṣṭim ivākurvann ity utprekṣitam | bhagavatā saha nanṛtuḥ | kva | bhramarā eva gāyakā yasyāṃ rāsasabhāyām ||BhPC_10,33.16||
body.translated_text: There, when the <s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, and other musicians and singers were overwhelmed and stupefied by the intensity of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic rapture), showing yet another abundance of music and the like, he describes the excitement of the <s>Rāsa</s> with 'With lotuses at the ears.' With lotuses at the ears, and with locks of hair as ornaments, and with cheeks, and with perspiration — on the faces, the beauty of those [<s>gopīs</s>] who possess such [features]. 'Bells' means small bells. With bracelets, anklets, and bells as instruments — as musical accompaniment. 'Whose garlands had fallen from their hair' — by this it is figuratively suggested that the hair, delighted by the rhythm and movement, showered flowers upon their feet as if making a rain of blossoms while shaking their heads. They danced together with the Lord. Where? In the <s>Rāsa</s> assembly where bees themselves were the singers. ||BhPC_10,33.16||

children.translated_text: Thus, with embraces, caresses, intimate glances, and unbridled playful laughter,
the Lord of <s>Ramā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) sported with the beauties of <s>Vraja</s>, like a child delighting in his own reflections. //

body.text: yathā gopyo nānāvibhramair bhagavatā saha vijahrur evaṃ bhagavān api svavilāsais tābhiḥ saha rema ity āha-evam iti | tadvilāsānabhibhūtasyaiva ratau dṛṣṭāntaḥ-yathārbhaka iti | svapratibimbair vibhramaḥ krīḍā yasya sa iva | anenaitad darśitam-svīyam eva sarvakalākauśalaṃ saugandhyalāvaṇyamādhuryādi ca tāsu sañcārya tābhiḥ saha reme yathārbhakaḥ svapratibimbair iti ||BhPC_10,33.17||
body.translated_text: Just as the <s>gopīs</s> sported with the Lord through various amorous gestures, so too the Lord sported with them through His own playfulness — he says this with 'Thus.' An illustration for His not being overwhelmed by their charms even during love-play — 'like a child.' Like one whose play (<s>vibhrama</s>) is with his own reflections. By this it is shown: having infused into them His own mastery of all arts, His fragrance, grace, and sweetness, He sported with them, just as a child [plays] with his own reflections. ||BhPC_10,33.17||

children.translated_text: Their senses bewildered by the joy of contact with His limbs, their hair, garments, and breast-bands —

children.text: nāñjaḥ prativyoḍhum alaṃ vrajastriyo visrastamālābharaṇāḥ kurūdvaha //
children.translated_text: the women of <s>Vraja</s> could not properly hold [these] in place, O descendant of <s>Kuru</s>, their garlands and ornaments having fallen away. //

body.text: tās tu bhagavadvilāsair ākulā babhūvur ity āha-tadaṅgeti | tasyāṅgasaṅgena prakṛṣṭām utprītis tayā ākulāny avaśānīndriyāṇi yāsāṃ tāḥ viślathabandhān keśādīn añjasā[*78] prativyoḍhuṃ yathāpūrvaṃ dhartuṃ nālaṃ na samarthā babhūvuḥ | visrastā mālā ābharaṇāni ca yāsāṃ tāḥ ||BhPC_10,33.18||
body.translated_text: They became overwhelmed by the Lord's playfulness — he says this with 'Their limbs.' By the contact with His limbs, the intense delight arising from it made their senses uncontrolled — those [<s>gopīs</s>] whose senses were thus overwhelmed were unable to properly hold in place, to restore as before, their loosened hair and other [adornments]. 'Whose garlands and ornaments had fallen away' — such were they. ||BhPC_10,33.18||

body.text: [*78] añjasā anusaṃdhānapūrvakam |
body.translated_text: [*78] 'Properly' means with due attention and care.

children.translated_text: Seeing the playful sport of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the celestial women became enraptured,
smitten with desire, and the moon along with his retinue of stars became astonished. //

body.text: na kevalaṃ tā evākulendriyāḥ kintu devyo 'pīty āha-kṛṣṇavikrīḍitam iti | kiṃ ca śaśāṅkaś ceti | anenaitat sūcitam-śaśāṅkena vismitena gatau vismṛtāyā tataḥ prāktanāḥ sarve 'pi grahās tatra tatraiva tasthus tataś cātidīrghāsu rātriṣu yathāsukhaṃ vijahrur iti ||BhPC_10,33.19||
body.translated_text: Not only they [the <s>gopīs</s>] had their senses overwhelmed, but even the celestial women — he says this with '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s play.' Furthermore, the moon [became astonished] — this indicates: the moon, being astonished, forgot its course, and therefore all the planets from before remained fixed in their positions, and thus during those exceedingly long nights, they sported at their leisure. ||BhPC_10,33.19||

children.translated_text: Having made Himself as many as the <s>gopī</s> women [present],

children.text: reme sa bhagavāṃs tābhir ātmārāmo 'pi līlayā //
children.translated_text: the Lord, though <s>ātmārāma</s> (self-delighting), sported with them as a play (<s>līlā</s>). //

body.text: kiṃ ca kṛtveti | ayaṃ bhāvaḥ-"kātyāyani mahāmāye mahāyoginy adhīśvari / nandagopasutaṃ devi patiṃ me kuru te namaḥ // "[*79] iti pratyekaṃ tābhiḥ prārthanād bhagavatāpi-"yātābalā vrajaṃ siddhā mayemā raṃsyatha kṣapāḥ / "[*80] iti tathaiva pratiśrutatvāt tāvantam ātmānaṃ kṛtvā reme iti | yāvatīr yāvatyaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.20||
body.translated_text: Furthermore, 'Having made' — the purport is: 'O <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, great <s>Māyā</s>, great <s>Yoginī</s>, supreme mistress! O goddess, make the son of <s>Nanda Gopa</s> my husband, salutations to you!' [*79] — since each of them had prayed thus individually, and since the Lord had likewise promised: 'Go, O women, to <s>Vraja</s>, your desires fulfilled; with me you shall enjoy these nights' [*80] — therefore, having made Himself equally many, He sported. 'As many as' means as many [as there were <s>gopīs</s>]. ||BhPC_10,33.20||

children.translated_text: Of those [<s>gopīs</s>] exhausted from excessive sport, He, the compassionate one,
lovingly wiped their faces, O <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Parīkṣit</s>), with His gentle hand. //

body.text: [*81] "tāsāṃ rativihāreṇa" iti pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*81] The reading '<s>tāsāṃ rativihāreṇa</s>' ('by amorous sport') is [also] attested.

body.text: kṛpātiśayam āha-tāsām iti ||BhPC_10,33.21||
body.translated_text: He describes the excess of [His] compassion with 'Of those.' ||BhPC_10,33.21||

children.translated_text: The <s>gopīs</s>, with the beauty of cheeks adorned by the luster of gleaming golden earrings and curling locks, with glances accompanied by nectarean smiles,

children.text: mānaṃ dadhatya ṛṣabhasya jaguḥ kṛtāni puṇyāni tatkararuhasparśapramodāḥ //
children.translated_text: honoring the best of men (<s>Ṛṣabha</s>), sang of His glorious deeds, delighted by the touch of His fingernails. //

body.text: tato 'tihṛṣṭānāṃ gopīnāṃ caritam āha-gopya iti | sphuratāṃ svarṇakuṇḍalānāṃ kuntalānāṃ ca tviṣā gaṇḍeṣu yā śrīs tayā sudhitenāmṛtāyitena hāsasahitena nirīkṣaṇena ca ṛṣabhasya patyuḥ kṛṣṇasya mānaṃ dadhatyaḥ pūjāṃ kurvatyas tatkarmāṇi jaguḥ | tasya kararuhair nakhaiḥ sparśena pramodo yāsāṃ tāḥ ||BhPC_10,33.22||
body.translated_text: Then he describes the conduct of the exceedingly delighted <s>gopīs</s> with '<s>gopīs</s>.' With the luster of gleaming golden earrings and curling locks on their cheeks, the beauty thereof, and with nectarean, ambrosial glances accompanied by laughter — honoring the best one (<s>Ṛṣabha</s>), their lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, offering worship — they sang of His deeds. Those whose delight came from the touch of His fingernails — such were they. ||BhPC_10,33.22||

children.text: tābhir yutaḥ śramam apohitum aṅgasaṅgaghṛṣṭasrajaḥ sa[*82] kucakuṅkumarañjitāyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Accompanied by them, to relieve His fatigue, His garland crushed by the close contact of their limbs, [its flowers] stained with the <s>kuṅkuma</s> saffron from their breasts,

children.text: gandharvapālibhir anudruta āviśad vāḥ śrānto gajībhir ibharāḍ iva bhinnasetuḥ //
children.translated_text: followed by <s>Gandharva</s> lords singing like bees, He entered the water, like the king of elephants, having broken the dam, [enters a river] fatigued, accompanied by she-elephants. //

body.text: [*82] "svakucakuṅkuma" iti pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*82] The reading '<s>svakucakuṅkuma</s>' ('the <s>kuṅkuma</s> from their own breasts') is [also] attested.

body.text: atha jalakelim āha-tābhir iti | tāsām aṅgasaṅgena ghṛṣṭā saṃmarditā yā srak tasyāḥ ata eva tāsāṃ kucakuṅkumena rañjitāyāḥ saṃbandhibhir gandharvapālibhir gandharvapā gandharvapataya iva gāyanto yo 'layas tair anudruto 'nugataḥ sa kṛṣṇo vāḥ udakam āviśat | bhinnasetur vidārita vapraḥ svayaṃ cātikrāntalokavedamaryādaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.23||
body.translated_text: Now he describes the water-sport with 'Accompanied by them.' His garland, crushed and pressed by the contact with their limbs — and therefore stained by the <s>kuṅkuma</s> from their breasts — followed by <s>Gandharva</s> lords, those whose lords are <s>Gandharvas</s>, [meaning] those singing like <s>Gandharva</s> masters, the bees [formed] a retinue that followed Him. That <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> entered the water. 'Having broken the dam' means having burst through the embankment — and He Himself had transcended the boundaries of worldly and Vedic convention. ||BhPC_10,33.23||

children.text: so 'mbhasy alaṃ yuvatibhiḥ pariṣicyamānaḥ premṇekṣitaḥ[*83] prahasatībhir itas tato 'ṅga /
children.translated_text: He, being splashed all around by the young women in the water, gazed upon with love by those who were laughing, O <s>Aṅga</s> (<s>Parīkṣit</s>),

children.text: vaimānikaiḥ kusumavarṣibhir īdyamāno reme svayaṃ svaratir[*84] atra gajendralīlaḥ //
children.translated_text: praised by the aerial beings who showered flowers, He sported, Himself self-delighting (<s>svarati</s>), with the playfulness of the king of elephants. //

body.text:
[*83] "premṇokṣitaḥ" ity api pāṭhaḥ |
[*84] svaratiḥ ātmārāmo 'pi, yadvā svāsu tāsu ratir yasya, kiṃ vā svā asādhāraṇī ratir jalakrīḍā yasya |
body.translated_text:
[*83] The reading '<s>premṇokṣitaḥ</s>' ('sprinkled with love') is also attested.
[*84] '<s>Svaratiḥ</s>' means '<s>ātmārāma</s>' (self-delighting); or, one whose delight (<s>rati</s>) is in them, His own [beloveds]; or, one whose own (<s>svā</s>) unique play (<s>rati</s>) is water-sport.

body.text: svaratir ātmārāmo 'pi atra gopīmaṇḍale 'mbhasi vā ||BhPC_10,33.24||
body.translated_text: 'Self-delighting (<s>svaratiḥ</s>)' means though He is <s>ātmārāma</s> (delighting in the Self), here, in this circle of <s>gopīs</s>, or in the water. ||BhPC_10,33.24||

children.translated_text: Then, in the garden of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, where the horizons were filled / with the fragrance-bearing breeze from flowers on water and land,

children.text: cacāra bhṛṅgapramadāgaṇāvṛto yathā madacyud dviradaḥ kareṇubhiḥ //
children.translated_text: He wandered, surrounded by swarms of bees and groups of women, / like a rut-exuding elephant among female elephants. //

body.text: sthalajalakrīḍe darśite vanakrīḍāṃ darśayati-tataś ceti | yamunāyā upavane jalasthalaprasūnānāṃ gandho yasmiṃs tenānilena juṣṭāni diśāṃ taṭāny antā yasmin | yadvā diśaś ca taṭaṃ sthalaṃ ca yasminn upavane | bhṛṅgāṇāṃ pramadānāṃ ca gaṇair āvṛtaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.25||
body.translated_text: Having shown water-play and land-play, he now shows forest-play with ‘tataś ca.’ In the garden by the <s>Yamunā</s>, where the horizons in all directions were filled by the breeze bearing the fragrance of flowers on water and land. Alternatively, ‘whose garden has directions, banks, and dry land.’ Surrounded by swarms of bees and groups of women. ||BhPC_10,33.25||

children.translated_text: Thus He, whose desires are ever fulfilled, accompanied by a group of loving women, / enjoyed nights illumined by the rays of the moon,
with erotic pleasure contained within Himself, / [nights that were] the abode of all the <s>rasas</s> (aesthetic sentiments) described in autumn poetry. //
