body.text: rāsakrīḍāṃ nigamayati-evam iti | sa kṛṣṇaḥ satyasaṅkalpo 'nurāgistrīkadambastha evaṃ sarvā niśāḥ sevitavān | śaratkāvyakathārasāśrayāḥ śaradi bhavāḥ kāvyeṣu kathyamānā ye rasās teṣām āśrayabhūtā niśāḥ | yadvā niśā iti dvitīyā 'tyantasaṃyoge | śṛṅgārarasāśrayāḥ śaradi[*85] prasiddhāḥ kāvyeṣu yāḥ kathās tāḥ siṣeve iti | evam apy ātmany evāvaruddhaḥ saurataś caramadhātur na tu skhalito yasyeti kāmajayoktiḥ ||BhPC_10,33.26|| ||BhPC_10,33.27||
body.translated_text: He concludes the <s>rāsa</s> sport with ‘evam.’ That <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose resolve is ever true, standing amid the throng of enamored women, thus enjoyed all those nights. ‘Nights that are the abode of the <s>rasas</s> described in poetry about autumn’ — nights that occur in autumn, which are the repositories of the <s>rasas</s> told in poems. Alternatively, ‘nights’ is in the accusative case of extended duration; He enjoyed the stories of the <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s> (erotic sentiment) famous in autumn[*85] in poems. Even so, ‘with erotic pleasure contained within Himself alone’ — the last element [of the compound indicates that] He did not waver. This is the statement of His conquest of desire. ||BhPC_10,33.26|| ||BhPC_10,33.27||

body.text: [*85] śaratkāvyakathāḥ śaradi sarvadeśakālakavibhir yāvatyo varṇayituṃ śakyante tāvatīḥ kathāḥ siṣeve ācacāra |
body.translated_text: [*85] ‘Autumn-poetry-stories’ — He enacted as many stories as all the poets of all lands and times could describe about autumn.

children.translated_text: How could He, who is the speaker, doer, and protector of the boundaries of <s>dharma</s>,
have practiced what is contrary [to <s>dharma</s>], O <s>brāhmaṇa</s> — the touching of others’ wives? //

body.text: pratīpaṃ pratikūlādharmam ity arthaḥ | ācarat kṛtavān | na cedam adharmamātraṃ kalañja-bhakṣaṇādivat kintu mahāsāhasam ity āha-paradārābhimarśanam iti ||BhPC_10,33.28||
body.translated_text: ‘Contrary’ means an adverse <s>adharma</s> — this is the meaning. ‘Practiced’ means did. And this is not mere <s>adharma</s> like eating prohibited food and the like; rather it is a great outrage — thus he says ‘the touching of others’ wives.’ ||BhPC_10,33.28||

children.translated_text: The lord of the <s>Yadus</s>, whose desires are fulfilled, / performed what is despicable.

children.text: kim abhiprāya etan naḥ saṃśayaṃ chindhi suvrata //
children.translated_text: With what intent? Resolve this doubt for us, O man of excellent vows! //

body.text: āptakāmasya nāyam adharma iti ced yady evaṃ kāmābhāvān ninditaṃ kenābhiprāyeṇa kṛtavān iti pṛcchati-āptakāma iti ||BhPC_10,33.29||
body.translated_text: If [one argues that] for one whose desires are fulfilled this is not <s>adharma</s>, then if so, since desire is absent, with what intent did He do what is condemned? — thus he asks with ‘āptakama.’ ||BhPC_10,33.29||

children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Śuka</s> said:
The transgression of <s>dharma</s> and the daring of the powerful[*86] / is seen [in many cases];

children.text: tejīyasāṃ na doṣāya vahneḥ[*87] sarvabhujo yathā //
children.translated_text: for the mighty, it does not result in fault, / just as fire[*87] that consumes everything [is not defiled]. //

body.text:
[*86] īśvarāṇāṃ karmādipāratantryahīnānām |
[*87] vahneḥ sarvabhuktvaṃ yathā nāpāvitryāyeti |
body.translated_text:
[*86] ‘Of the powerful’ — of those free from subjection to <s>karma</s> and the like.
[*87] The all-consuming nature of fire does not [result in] impurity, just so.

body.text: parameśvare kaimutikanyāyena parihartuṃ sāmānyato mahatāṃ vṛttam āha-dharmavyatikrama iti | sāhasaṃ ca dṛṣṭaṃ prajāpatīndrasomaviśvāmitrādīnām | tac ca teṣāṃ tejasvināṃ doṣāya na bhavatīti ||BhPC_10,33.30||
body.translated_text: To resolve [the question] regarding the Supreme Lord by the argument ‘how much more so,’ he first states the general conduct of the great: ‘<s>dharma</s>-transgression.’ Daring is seen [in the cases of] <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, and others. And that does not lead to fault for those powerful ones. ||BhPC_10,33.30||

children.text: naitat samācarej jātu manasāpi hy anīśvaraḥ /
children.translated_text: One who is not a lord should never practice this, / not even in thought;

children.text: vinaśyaty ācaran mauḍhyād yathā rudro 'bdhijaṃ viṣam //
children.translated_text: acting thus out of delusion, one perishes, / just as one other than <s>Rudra</s> [would perish from drinking] the ocean-born poison. //

body.text: tarhi "yad yad ācarati śreṣṭhaḥ" iti nyāyenānyo 'pi kuryād ity āśaṅkyāha-naitad iti | anīśvaro dehādiparatantraḥ yathā rudravyatirikto viṣam ācaran bhakṣayan ||BhPC_10,33.31||
body.translated_text: Then, anticipating the objection that ‘Whatever the great one does, [others follow]’ — he says ‘na etat.’ ‘Not a lord’ means one subject to the body and the rest; just as someone other than <s>Rudra</s>, consuming, eating the poison, [would perish]. ||BhPC_10,33.31||

children.translated_text: The words of the lords are true, and their conduct is true in some cases.

children.text: teṣāṃ yat svavacoyuktaṃ buddhimāṃs tat samācaret //
children.translated_text: What is consistent with their own words — that a wise person should follow. //

body.text: kathaṃ tarhi sadācārasya prāmāṇyam ata āha-īśvarāṇām iti | teṣāṃ vacaḥ satyam, atas tad uktam ācared eva | ācaritaṃ tu kvacit satyam | ataḥ svavacoyuktaṃ teṣāṃ vacasā yadyad yuktam aviruddhaṃ tattad evācaret ||BhPC_10,33.32||
body.translated_text: How then is the authority of right conduct [to be determined]? To this he says with ‘īśvarāṇām.’ Their words are true; therefore one should indeed follow what they have said. But their conduct is true only in some cases. Therefore one should follow only that which is consistent with their words, that which is not contradicted [by their teachings]. ||BhPC_10,33.32||

body.text:
BhP_10,33.33
kuśalācaritenaiṣām iha svārtho na vidyate / viparyayeṇa vānartho nirahaṅkāriṇāṃ prabho //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,33.33
For those who are free from ego, O lord, there is no personal gain / from virtuous conduct here, nor harm from its opposite. //

body.text: nanu tarhi te 'pi kim evaṃ sāhasam ācaranti tatrāha-kuśaleti | prārabdhakarmakṣapaṇamātram eva teṣāṃ kṛtyaṃ nānyad ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.33||
body.translated_text: Now then, why do even they perform such daring acts? To this he says with ‘kuśala.’ The only purpose for them is the exhaustion of their <s>prārabdhakarma</s> (karma already in effect) and nothing else — this is the meaning. ||BhPC_10,33.33||

body.text:
BhP_10,33.34
kim[*88] utākhilasattvānāṃ tiryaṅmartyadivaukasām / īśituś ceśitavyānāṃ kuśalākuśalānvayaḥ //
body.translated_text:
BhP_10,33.34
How much less[*88] could there be any connection with good or evil / for the Lord of all beings — animals, humans, and celestials — / [who is] the ruler of all that is to be ruled? //

body.text: [*88] yadā īśitavyānāṃ niyamyānāṃ nirahaṅkāriṇāṃ jīvānāṃ kuśalākuśalānvayo na vidyate tadā tiryagādirūpāṇām akhilasattvānām īśitur niyantuḥ kuśalākuśalānvayo na vidyata iti kim u vaktavyam iti pūrvaślokasthena "na vidyate" iti padasaṃbandhenānvayaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*88] When for the governed, the regulated, the egoless individual souls there is no connection with good and evil, then what need to say that for the Lord who is the ruler of all beings in the forms of animals and the rest, there is no connection with good and evil? — the construction is with the phrase ‘na vidyate’ from the previous verse.

body.text: prastutam āha-kim uteti | kuśalākuśalānvayo na vidyata iti kiṃ punar vaktavyam ity arthaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.34||
body.translated_text: He states what is being discussed with ‘kim uta.’ The connection with good and evil does not exist — what more need be said? This is the meaning. ||BhPC_10,33.34||

children.translated_text: Those who are satisfied by serving the pollen of His lotus feet, / whose bonds of all <s>karma</s> have been destroyed by the power of <s>yoga</s>,

children.text: svairaṃ caranti munayo 'pi na nahyamānās tasyecchayāttavapuṣaḥ kuta eva bandhaḥ //
children.translated_text: even sages roam freely, unfettered — / how then could there be bondage for Him who has assumed a body by His own will? //

body.text: etad eva sphuṭīkaroti-yasya pādapaṅkajaparāgasya niṣevaṇena tṛptāḥ, yadvā yasya pādapaṅkajaparāge niṣevā yeṣāṃ te ca te tṛptāś ceti bhaktā ity arthaḥ | tathā jñāninaś ca na nahyamānā bandhanam aprāptavantaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.35||
body.translated_text: He clarifies this point: ‘Those who are satisfied through the service of the pollen of His lotus feet’ — or ‘those whose devotion is [directed] toward the pollen of His lotus feet, and who are satisfied’ — meaning devotees. And likewise the knowers [of <s>Brahman</s>] too, ‘unfettered’ — having not attained bondage. ||BhPC_10,33.35||

children.text: gopīnāṃ tatpatīnāṃ ca sarveṣām eva dehinām /
children.translated_text: He who moves within the <s>gopīs</s>, their husbands, and indeed / all embodied beings — that Overseer,
He has assumed a body here as sport. //

body.text: paradāratvaṃ gopīnām aṅgīkṛtya parihṛtam, idānīṃ bhagavataḥ sarvāntaryāmiṇaḥ paradārasevā nāma na kācid ity āha-gopīnām iti | yo 'ntaś caraty adhyakṣo buddhyādisākṣī sa eva krīḍanena dehabhāk, na tv asmadāditulyo yena doṣaḥ syād iti ||BhPC_10,33.36||
body.translated_text: Having accepted the premise that the <s>gopīs</s> are others’ wives and resolved [the objection], now [he says]: for the <s>Bhagavān</s> who is the inner controller of all, there is no such thing as ‘intimacy with others’ wives’ — thus he says with ‘gopīnām.’ He who moves within [all beings], the Overseer, the witness of intellect and the rest — He Himself is the one who assumes a body through sport, not one comparable to us, by which there would be fault. ||BhPC_10,33.36||

children.translated_text: For the grace of beings[*89], having assumed a human body, / He engages in such sports

children.text: bhajate tādṛśīḥ krīḍā yāḥ śrutvā[*90] tatparo bhavet //
children.translated_text: that one who hears[*90] of them becomes devoted to Him. //

body.text:
[*89] "bhaktānām" iti pāṭhaḥ |
[*90] "smṛtvā" iti pāṭhaḥ |
body.translated_text:
[*89] Alternative reading: ‘of devotees.’
[*90] Alternative reading: ‘remembers.’

body.text: nanv evaṃ ced āptakāmasya nindite kutaḥ pravṛttir ity ata āha-anugrahāyeti | śṛṅgāra-rasākṛṣṭacetaso 'tibahirmukhān api svaparān kartum iti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.37||
body.translated_text: Now, if so, what is the reason for the activity of the desire-fulfilled one in something condemned? To this he says with ‘anugrahāya.’ The purport is: to attract even those extremely outward-turned people whose minds are drawn to the <s>śṛṅgāra-rasa</s> (erotic sentiment), and make them His own. ||BhPC_10,33.37||

children.text: nāsūyan khalu kṛṣṇāya mohitās tasya māyayā /
children.translated_text: The men of <s>Vraja</s>, deluded by His <s>māyā</s> (divine illusion), / did not feel jealousy toward <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,

children.text: manyamānāḥ svapārśvasthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ //
children.translated_text: thinking that their own respective wives were by their sides. //

body.text: nanv anye 'pi bhinnācārāḥ svaceṣṭitam evam eveti vadanti tatrāha-nāsūyann iti | evaṃbhūtaiśvaryābhāve tathā kurvantaḥ pāpā jñeyā iti bhāvaḥ ||BhPC_10,33.38||
body.translated_text: Now [one may say:] ‘Others too whose conduct is transgressive [may claim] that their own behavior was just like this.’ To this he says with ‘nāsūyan.’ The purport is: those who act thus without possessing such lordly power should be considered sinful. ||BhPC_10,33.38||

children.translated_text: When the night of <s>Brahmā</s> was over, permitted by <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
the <s>gopīs</s>, dear to the <s>Bhagavān</s>[*91], went unwillingly to their own homes. //

body.text: [*91] bhagavān priyo yāsāṃ, bhagavato vā priyāḥ |
body.translated_text: [*91] Those for whom <s>Bhagavān</s> is dear; or those who are dear to <s>Bhagavān</s>.

body.text: brahmarātre brāhme muhūrte upāvṛtte prāpte ||BhPC_10,33.39||
body.translated_text: When the night of <s>Brahmā</s> — meaning when the <s>brāhma muhūrta</s> (auspicious pre-dawn hour) — had arrived. ||BhPC_10,33.39||

children.text: vikrīḍitaṃ vrajavadhūbhir idaṃ ca viṣṇoḥ śraddhānvito 'nuśṛṇuyād atha varṇayed yaḥ /
children.translated_text: Whoever with faith hears or narrates this sport / of <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the young women of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: bhaktiṃ parāṃ bhagavati pratilabhya kāmaṃ hṛdrogam āśv apahinoty acireṇa dhīraḥ //
children.translated_text: attaining supreme <s>bhakti</s> (devotion) to the <s>Bhagavān</s>, / that steadfast one quickly casts off the heart’s disease of desire (<s>kāma</s>). //

body.text: bhagavataḥ kāmavijayarūparāsakrīḍāśravaṇādeḥ kāmavijayam eva phalam āha-vikrīḍitam iti | acireṇa dhīraḥ san hṛdrogaṃ kāmam[*92] āśu apahinoti parityajatīti ||BhPC_10,33.40||
body.translated_text: The fruit of hearing and so forth of the <s>Bhagavān</s>’s <s>rāsa</s> sport, which has the nature of the conquest of desire, is indeed the conquest of desire itself — he states with ‘vikrīḍitam.’ ‘Becoming steadfast, he quickly casts off the heart’s disease of desire (<s>kāma</s>)[*92].’ ||BhPC_10,33.40||

body.text: [*92] yadvā kāmaṃ yatheṣṭaṃ āśu bhaktiṃ labdhvā kāmādisarvahṛdrogam acireṇa hinotīty arthaḥ |
body.translated_text: [*92] Alternatively, ‘kāmam’ means ‘as one wishes’; having quickly attained <s>bhakti</s>, one removes in a short time all heart-diseases including desire — this is the meaning.

children.translated_text: This commentary, the <s>Bhāvārthadipīkā</s> on the <s>Śrī Bhāgavatam</s>, taking the tenth [book] as its basis, / was composed by <s>Śrī Śrīdhara</s>, servant of <s>Śrī Paramānanda</s>. // 1 //
[continuation of the colophon verse]

body.text: iti śrīmadbhāgavate mahāpurāṇe daśamaskandhe pūrvārdhe bhāvārthadīpikāyāṃ ṭīkāyāṃ trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ **33**
body.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Bhāgavata Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the tenth book, first half, in the commentary called <s>Bhāvārthadipīkā</s>, the thirty-third chapter. **33**
